| [THEORY-509](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-509.md) | Under genericity conditions, two dense or top-k (k ≥ 2) mixture-of-experts layers compute the same function only if they differ by a permutation of the experts with their gates and a common translation of the gate weights, and the translation leaves every interpolation barrier unchanged, so expert order is the only gate symmetry alignment must undo | Tran, Trinh, Bui & Nguyen (2025), [LIT-670](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-670.md), read in [NOTE-513](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-513.md). Softmax is invariant to a common shift of scores and the sum to the order of terms, so G(n) = ℝ^d × ℝ × S_n preserves the layer; Theorems 4.1–4.2 show that generically it is all of the gate's symmetry, for dense gating and for top-k with k ≥ 2 (top-1 has an extra scaling). Aligning expert order and then each expert's hidden units gives barriers of 0.0044–0.0066 between GPT-2 MoE layers fine-tuned from different seeds, against 0.14–0.86 without the order step. Every experiment shares and freezes the backbone around the inserted layer, so it is not evidence about independently trained MoE models. | Active |
| [THEORY-513](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-513.md) | Observational entropy taken relative to a maximum-entropy prior τ, S(τ) − D_M(ρ‖τ), lies between S(ρ) and S(τ) for states meeting the prior's constraint, is finite and continuous whenever S(τ) is, and reduces to about two dozen textbook entropies by choice of measurement and prior; its second laws are bounds on the time-averaged state's divergence from the prior, proved small only under sufficient conditions (nondegenerate energy gaps for equilibration, the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis for fit to the prior) | Schindler, Strasberg, Galke, Winter & Jabbour (2025), [LIT-082](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-082.md), read in full in [NOTE-043](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-043.md), with Proofs 1, 2, 7, 10 and 11 checked line by line. The bounds, the special cases and the decomposition are proved. The central target, a small divergence of the time-averaged state from the prior, is proved for no concrete system; in the paper's own examples "in none of those cases was the smallness proved here analytically" (p. 12). Unpublished as of the reading. | Active |
| [THEORY-515](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-515.md) | Sampling a posterior p(x\|y) when only joint samples (X, Y) can be drawn is solved by a Schrödinger bridge on the joint space, with y held fixed along the path, between the joint distribution and any reference sharing its y-marginal; the bridge averages the per-observation bridges, its first iterative-proportional-fitting step is the conditional score-based model, and the error of later steps at the data end falls as 1/n times the reference's distance from the bridge | Shi, De Bortoli, Deligiannidis & Doucet (2022), [LIT-776](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-776.md), read in [NOTE-589](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-589.md). Propositions 1–3 are proofs, read for structure and not checked line by line. The empirical gains over the conditional score model hold at equal, small step counts on most but not all image metrics, and in Lorenz-63 filtering at 20 steps. That a long noising horizon is not what makes conditional diffusion correct is [NOTE-589](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-589.md)'s interpretation, not something the paper tests. | Active |
| [THEORY-516](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-516.md) | For any presheaf of propositions over a small category of contexts, a sieve-valued valuation satisfies the generalized functional-composition condition exactly when it is a subobject of that presheaf, and the construction runs unchanged in classical physics, where every microstate gives a global section yet truth values are still non-Boolean sieves; so the logic of the truth values is fixed by the base category, not by whether a presheaf has global sections | Butterfield & Isham (1998), [LIT-381](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-381.md), read in full in [NOTE-329](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-329.md): Theorem 4.1 proves that generalized FUNC is exactly naturality of ν : G → Ω, for any presheaf G of posets on any small category. In classical physics the value presheaf has a global section per microstate (3.6–3.7), yet the macrostate and microstate valuations are sieve-valued, and [NOTE-329](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-329.md) shows excluded middle failing at a microstate. Isham & Butterfield (1999), [LIT-389](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-389.md) ([NOTE-334](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-334.md)), adds that Ω is unique for a given topos and that a base with one arrow between any two objects gives two-valued logic. The choice of base, and so of the logic, remains free. | Active |
| [THEORY-519](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-519.md) | Supervised learners compose only once each carries a request function that passes a corrected input upstream; with it they form a symmetric monoidal category, and for a fixed step size and an error whose derivative in its first argument is invertible, gradient descent with backpropagation is a faithful strong symmetric monoidal functor into it from differentiable parametrised functions | Fong, Spivak & Tuyéras (2017; LICS 2019), [LIT-827](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-827.md), read in full in [NOTE-625](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-625.md), which followed the chain-rule proof of Theorem A.1 line by line. Learners (P, I, U, r) form Learn (Prop. II.4); Theorem III.2 makes gradient descent with backpropagation a functor Para → Learn. Covered: fixed step size, one datum per update, deterministic updates, and errors with invertible ∂e/∂x, which excludes cross-entropy at 0 and 1. That learners cannot compose without a request is argued, not proved. Learn says how learners compose, not whether they learn. | Active |
| [THEORY-522](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-522.md) | Open text-to-image diffusion models of 2022–2023 render a single named object almost always but fail most on relative position and next on attribute binding, by human rating and by detector checks alike; scaling the image model or continuing pretraining does not fix position, and interactions are rated near ceiling only by rubrics that ask whether an action is depicted | GenEval (Ghosh, Hajishirzi & Schmidt 2023, [LIT-782](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-782.md), [NOTE-593](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-593.md)) and T2I-CompBench with its journal extension (Huang et al. 2023 and 2025, [LIT-783](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-783.md) and [LIT-798](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-798.md), [NOTE-592](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-592.md) and [NOTE-610](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-610.md)), two independent benchmarks that do not cite each other. GenEval: single object 0.97–0.98 for every diffusion model, position at most 0.15, binding at most 0.35. Human ratings in T2I-CompBench: 2D spatial 0.31–0.46, shape binding 0.51–0.70, interactions 0.81–0.99. Human ratings cover only six 2023-era models; the 2024–25 generation is ranked by automatic judges validated on the older ones, so the ordering is not established for it. | Active |
| [THEORY-524](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-524.md) | On cyclic measurement scenarios, where the contexts' overlaps form one chordless N-cycle, the ℤ/2 Čech obstruction computed on the (N−1)-th iterated joint model is exact for logical and strong contextuality, the bound N − 1 being tight; beyond cycles no such result is established, the published extension is false on its own example, and the completeness conjecture fails on a Kochen–Specker cover that is never detected at any level | Carù (2018), [LIT-280](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-280.md), read in [NOTE-253](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-253.md), and the same result republished as Thm IV.32 of Carù's 2019 thesis, [LIT-281](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-281.md), read in [NOTE-254](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-254.md). The cyclic theorem is proved and was confirmed on Hardy, on the (2,2,4) counterexample and on 659 random contextual cycle models. The failures beyond cycles (Prop 8.2 / IV.34, the §8 cover, Conjecture 9.1 / IV.41) are the readers' computations and a lifting lemma, not the author's. The joint models grow exponentially; nothing analyses the cost. | Active |
| [THEORY-526](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-526.md) | The Čech cohomology obstruction of a support section is a sound but incomplete witness of contextuality: it vanishes exactly when the section lies in a compatible family of integer combinations of support sections, so it is non-zero on every section of every All-vs-Nothing model, over any coefficient ring, on a connected cover, yet it misses the Hardy model entirely, part of a strongly contextual Kochen–Specker cover, and every section of a strongly contextual model on the fully symmetric (2,2,4) Bell cover | Abramsky, Mansfield & Barbosa (2011), [LIT-277](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-277.md) ([NOTE-250](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-250.md)); Abramsky, Barbosa, Kishida, Lal & Mansfield (2015), [LIT-278](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-278.md) ([NOTE-251](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-251.md)); Carù (2017), [LIT-279](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-279.md) ([NOTE-252](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-252.md)). The criterion (Prop 4.2 / Prop 16) and the All-vs-Nothing theorem (Thm 21) are proved; the three failures are explicit models, which the readers re-computed exactly over ℤ and ℤ/2. Two steps are the readers': that the §8 cover and the (2,2,4) model admit no All-vs-Nothing argument over any ring, by Thm 21 read contrapositively. The witness is possibilistic, so it cannot grade anything below strong contextuality. | Active |
| [THEORY-530](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-530.md) | The spectrum of a matrix bounds the norm of its rational functions up to a constant only if the matrix is diagonalisable, with the eigenvector condition number as the constant, while the closed numerical range of any Hilbert-space operator does so with a universal constant between 2 and 11.08, exactly 2 for 2×2 matrices | Badea & Beckermann (2013), [LIT-011](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-011.md), a handbook survey read in full in [NOTE-009](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-009.md). Example 107.2.5: σ(A) is K-spectral iff A is diagonalisable, with K ≤ cond(V). Fact 107.7.2: the closure of W(A) is completely K-spectral for every bounded A with a universal K ∈ [2, 11.08], and 2 suffices for 2×2. The chapter proves almost nothing itself; the numerical range result is cited to Crouzeix (2007). The bound 11.08 was the 2013 state; a later improvement to 1 + √2 is recalled in the reading but not verified. Whether the constant is 2 was open. | Active |
| [THEORY-534](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-534.md) | The optimality of maximum likelihood was never one theorem: each historical proof holds under conditions its author left implicit, and of the classical counterexamples the practically important one is a parameter count growing with the sample, while Hodges-type superefficiency is confined to a set of measure zero | Stigler (2007), [LIT-044](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-044.md), read in full in [NOTE-074](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-074.md). Fisher's 1922 proof rests on sufficiency, his 1925 proof on exact normality, and his private 1930 proof on multinomial data and smooth degree-0 estimators. Rigorous treatments (Wald 1943, Cramér 1946) came at the cost of unwieldy conditions. Neyman–Scott, where the MLE of σ² tends to σ²/2, is the failure Stigler weighs as practical; Hodges's superefficiency is possible only on a Lebesgue-null set (Le Cam 1953). It is a history: the theorem statements are reconstructions, and it says nothing about modern overparameterized models beyond one hedged warning. | Active |
| [THEORY-543](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-543.md) | Diffusion can destabilise a homogeneous steady state of reacting chemicals that is stable without it: a disturbance of one finite wave-length grows while uniform and very short ones decay, so a stationary pattern appears whose spacing is set by the reaction and diffusion constants and only its phase by the disturbance; with two substances this needs them to diffuse at different rates, and the pattern lasts only while free energy is supplied | Turing (1952), [LIT-535](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-535.md), read in full in [NOTE-427](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-427.md), with Cross & Hohenberg (1993), [LIT-527](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-527.md), skimmed in [NOTE-418](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-418.md). The linear analysis on a ring gives exact conditions (9.4a, b) for stationary waves of finite wave-length; that equal diffusibilities cannot satisfy them is [NOTE-427](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-427.md)'s substitution, not stated in the paper. Turing calls the linearity assumption "a serious one" and the biological examples "very limited". Stationary chemical Turing patterns were first made in 1989–1991, and real morphogens implementing the mechanism had not been identified by 1993. | Active |
| [THEORY-544](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-544.md) | In homotopy type theory extended with a strict directed interval and a layer of shapes, one contractibility condition, the Segal condition, gives a type identities, associativity and three-dimensional coherence, makes every function between Segal types a functor, and yields a dependent Yoneda lemma for covariant families; that such types are (∞,1)-categories rests on a semantics only sketched | Riehl & Shulman (2017), [LIT-032](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-032.md), read in full in [NOTE-069](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-069.md). The internal results of §§5–11 are proved: associativity from the Segal condition applied to A^2 (Prop. 5.9), inner 3-horns (Prop. 5.21), functoriality of every function (Prop. 6.1), the dependent Yoneda lemma (Thm 9.5), and uniqueness of left adjoints into a Segal type from a Rezk type (Thm 11.23). Segal and Rezk types match Segal and complete Segal spaces (Props A.21, A.25), but soundness of the type theory in bisimplicial sets is sketched and depends on an unproved initiality theorem. Coherence in all dimensions is conjectured, not proved. | Active |
| [THEORY-545](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-545.md) | Aerts and Gabora's founding quantum model of concepts is a classical probability model written in a Hilbert space: every context it uses is a projector diagonal in one basis, so the contexts commute and generate a Boolean algebra, its entangled 'pet fish' state gives the same statistics as a classically correlated mixture for every context in the model, and its guppy weights are copied from single-concept ratings rather than predicted for the conjunction | Aerts & Gabora (2005), Parts II and I, [LIT-312](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-312.md) and [LIT-340](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-340.md), read in [NOTE-299](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-299.md) and [NOTE-294](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-294.md). The structural facts are checks of the published model, not of the authors' prose: contexts are sums of basis projectors, counts are chosen to match rounded frequencies, and the authors call the result a "quantization" of a set-theoretical model. Part I's mark of non-classicality (eq. 19) is met by Boolean projection lattices too, and its lattice structure is supposed, not derived. The model as printed is also infeasible in two cells. It does not say that no quantum model of concepts does better. | Active |
| [THEORY-550](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-550.md) | Unsupervised clustering is not made epistemically superior to supervised classification by the absence of labels: it is sensitive to sample bias, highly sensitive to how inputs are represented, and overfits, with the number of clusters acting as a capacity control just as parametric complexity does in supervised learning | Søgaard (2024), [LIT-162](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-162.md), read in [NOTE-108](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-108.md). A rebuttal of two arguments for clustering's superiority, the No-Bias Argument and the Simplicity-Truth Argument, by toy counterexample and by the technical literature on overfitting in unsupervised learning (Hansen & Larsen 1996). The negative claims are firm. The paper's positive step, that supervised classification is "at least as" justified, is under-argued and is not part of this account. | Active |
| [THEORY-552](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-552.md) | Indeed's US software-development job-postings index rose to 233.8 in February 2022 and fell to 65.2 by mid-February 2025, measured against 1 February 2020 = 100, while all postings stood near 110; it was the deepest fall of any Indeed sector, though not the only one to have more than doubled, and the postings data cannot apportion the fall among interest rates, over-hiring and AI | Orosz (2025), [LIT-089](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-089.md), read in full in [NOTE-039](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-039.md), which checked the figures against Indeed Hiring Lab's own published series (current vintage). The headline numbers reproduce: 65.2 on 2025-02-13, a 3.59× fall from the peak, −8.3% year on year, all postings 109.5. Several side claims do not: the baseline is 1 February 2020, not January; the peak was February 2022, not mid-2022; six sectors peaked above 200. The index counts active postings, not vacancies or hires, and the post's ranking of causes is informal. | Active |
| [THEORY-553](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-553.md) | In the Döring–Isham topos representation of quantum theory a bounded physical quantity cannot take values in the topos's real-number object; it is represented faithfully by an arrow from the spectral presheaf to a presheaf of monotone real functions over subcontexts, so its value at a context is a spread that widens as the context shrinks, and these values form only a commutative monoid, under which sums of daseinised quantities are not daseinisations of sums | Döring & Isham, paper III (2007/8), [LIT-299](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-299.md) ([NOTE-290](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-290.md)), restated with additions in [LIT-378](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-378.md) ([NOTE-326](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-326.md)). The Gel'fand transforms of daseinised operators grow as contexts shrink, so arrows into the constant presheaf ℝ are impossible (3.3–3.4). Each Â gives a natural transformation δ̆^o(A) : Σ → ℝ^⪰ (Thm 3.1), and Â ↦ δ̆^o(A) is injective, by de Groote's results. ℝ^⪰ is a monoid, not a group; differences need a group completion, whose global elements are the functions of bounded variation on the context poset. No choice among the candidate value objects is made, and the state-dependent reading of the spread is cited, not proved. | Active |
| [THEORY-555](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-555.md) | In London in 2018, Airbnb listings that were possibly breaking the 90-night short-let cap, defined as entire homes offered for more than 180 days a year by hosts with two or more listings, were about 0.16% of the housing stock (about 5,300 homes) but 3.5–7% in a few central small areas, and across small areas they correlate weakly with flats, private renting and low dwelling-type diversity | Shabrina, Arcaute & Batty (2021), [LIT-094](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-094.md), read in full in [NOTE-071](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-071.md). A descriptive estimate from Inside Airbnb and VOA counts under a proxy that rests on availability, not bookings, and on an untested 50% occupancy. The abstract's "more than 2% ... misused" is the share listed at all, not the share possibly misused. The paper's borough rent result (n = 33, cross-sectional) and its "8% per doubling" translation do not belong to this account and should not be cited as an effect size. | Active |
| [THEORY-559](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-559.md) | In Kolmogorovian probability, joint distributedness is transitive, so representing a measurement by one random variable in every context it occurs in already puts all measurements of a connected system on one probability space; within that representation a Kochen–Specker or Bell contradiction refutes the context-independent identification of measurements, not the existence of a joint distribution | Dzhafarov & Kujala (2017), [LIT-836](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-836.md), read in full in [NOTE-623](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-623.md). The transitivity step is an elementary proof; the reading of the reductio is an argument that rests on it. It binds the random-variable representation only: the sheaf account keeps one variable per measurement and asks whether marginals glue, and a reader who holds that view is not bound by it. The paper also proves that a coupling of a binary connection is multimaximal iff adjacent pairs, ordered by their means, are maximally coupled (Theorem II.3). | Active |
| [THEORY-566](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-566.md) v2 | In Ganea et al.'s hyperbolic neural networks, linear maps and nonlinearities are Euclidean ones read through the chart at the origin, so a stack of them without biases is a Euclidean network conjugated by that chart, and the curvature acts only through the bias translations and the distance-based output layer | Ganea, Bécigneul & Hofmann (2018), [LIT-879](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-879.md), read in [NOTE-686](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-686.md), which checked the closed forms numerically. Möbius layers are defined as exp₀ ∘ f ∘ log₀, so any composition of them is exp₀ ∘ (the Euclidean composition) ∘ log₀, as the paper notes; only the Möbius bias, which is parallel transport from the origin followed by the exponential map, and the hyperbolic logistic regression's distances to geodesic hyperplanes are not absorbed by the chart. The structural fact is proved; that the networks' gains, confined to a synthetic task and to separating WordNet subtrees in low-dimensional Poincaré embeddings, come from those two operations is this record's inference. [NOTE-686](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-686.md) filed no THEORY. | Active |
| [THEORY-567](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-567.md) | In the donation game, where a cooperator pays c for another to get b, defectors win in a well-mixed population, and each of five mechanisms makes cooperators evolutionarily stable above a benefit-to-cost threshold: kin selection r > c/b, direct reciprocity w > c/b, indirect reciprocity q > c/b, network reciprocity b/c > k and group selection b/c > 1 + n/m; the rules cover altruism only, not mutualism, coordination or conflict | Nowak (2006), [LIT-501](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-501.md), read in [NOTE-409](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-409.md), main text only. A four-page review that casts each known mechanism as a 2×2 game so that one set of criteria applies to all. The five ESS conditions are confirmed by the main text; the derivations are in the supporting material, which was not read, and in cited papers. Several rules hold only under weak selection, regular graphs or rare group splitting. Every mechanism is modelled with the donation game, so mutualism, coordination and conflict are outside it. | Active |
| [THEORY-568](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-568.md) | Whatever redundancy measure a partial information decomposition uses, provided its atoms satisfy the consistency equation, the average number of single sources an atom can be read from is Σᵢ I(Xᵢ;Y)/I(X;Y) and the average number of sources it cannot do without is Σⱼ I(Xⱼ;Y\|X₋ⱼ)/I(X;Y); so the redundancy–synergy index equals (r̄ − 1)·I(X;Y), and for three or more sources it counts a k-way redundancy k − 1 times but synergy once | Gutknecht et al. (2025), [LIT-042](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-042.md), read in full in [NOTE-045](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-045.md), with the combinatorial proofs of Props. 1–4 and 6 checked by hand. The averages need only the consistency equation and I(X;Y) > 0; reading them as average degrees, and the bounds of Appendix B, need non-negative atoms. Corollary 5 overstates Prop. 6 (⇔ for ⇐). The network results are on tiny quantised models evaluated on their own training sets, and are not part of this account. | Active |
| [THEORY-569](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-569.md) | Measured as the contrast between a set of explanantia's CohOG+ coherence with the explanandum and with its negation, explanatory power satisfies Roche and Sober's Two Likelihood Inequalities for single hypotheses and fails the One, and in one causal chain and one collider it ranks the richer set above the sparser over a range of priors, where no two-place TLI measure can rank a conjunction so | Hartmann & Trpin (2026), [LIT-165](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-165.md), read in [NOTE-168](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-168.md), which recomputed all three numerical claims. One theorem (TLI for singleton explanans sets), one counterexample (OLI fails) and two parameterised existence examples (a distal cause for P(H1) < .7; a negatively interacting cause for P(H1) = P(H2) < .75). The escape from Roche & Sober is representational: a set is scored differently from the conjunction, and the two-place theorems still hold for conjunctions. No characterisation says when the richer set wins, and the paper's claim that the measure "accommodates key scientific judgments" is more than the body shows. | Active |
| [THEORY-574](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-574.md) | The structural width of Xin Li's learning programme is a covering number of the margin-safe region by local pieces: its lower bounds come from metric confinement through a wedge point, not from topology, labels enter only through the margin, and the error floor below width binds only learners assembled from local experts, so it does not entail routing, nor training routing apart from the task loss | Li (2026), [LIT-376](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-376.md) (Local Urysohn Width, v1), [LIT-375](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-375.md) (Structural Learning Theory) and [LIT-374](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-374.md) (Structural Decoupling), read jointly in [NOTE-323](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-323.md), [NOTE-324](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-324.md) and [NOTE-322](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-322.md). In repaired form the formal core holds: width is incomparable with the per-cell VC dimension, fewer cells than width give an error floor (under an assumption that states it), and discovering all basins costs Ω(w log w) samples. But local correctness is automatic on any connected patch, the bouquet lower bound is metric (the paper's Remark 8.11 concedes it), a global classifier has width 1 (Remark 3.4), and the additive Rademacher bound said to call for decoupled training holds for joint training too. | Active |
| [THEORY-576](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-576.md) | In a bundled network, one fiber graph attached at a single node to every node of a base graph, the low Laplacian spectrum is the base spectrum divided by the fiber size to first order, so the gap exponent (Fiedler dimension) is set by the base while the density-of-states exponent (spectral dimension) is the fiber's; the two come apart generically and coincide only in special cases, and relaxation then decays with the spectral dimension at intermediate times but equilibrates on a time set by the Fiedler dimension | Grimaldi, Villegas, Vezzani, Burioni, Cassi & Gabrielli (2025; PRE Letter 2026), [LIT-028](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-028.md), read in full with its SM in [NOTE-005](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-005.md), which re-derived the key steps and checked them numerically on the comb. λ_{n1} = ℓ^b_{n1}/N_f gives d_g = 2(d_f,f + d_f,b)/(d_f,f + 2d_f,b/d_g,b) in the base-controlled regime; d_s = d_s,f is earlier work by the same group. The comb has d_s = 1 and d_g = 4/3. Proved for one graph class only; the paper's composite finite-size scaling prefactors (SM Eqs. 25, 29) are wrong, and its "generic property of composite architectures" outruns the proof. | Active |
| [THEORY-581](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-581.md) v2 | Two exactly consistent descriptions of one system, at different scales and with equal past–future mutual information, can differ in how that information divides between redundancy and synergy; in small generated Boolean networks under the Williams–Beer redundancy measure the coarser scale was more synergy-biased in every random stochastic system, by at most about 0.07, and the direction mostly reversed for redundancy-biased deterministic ones | Varley & Hoel (2022), [LIT-027](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-027.md), read in [NOTE-020](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-020.md). Expanding a 3-node macroscale TPM into 4- and 5-node equivalence-class microscales holds mutual information fixed with zero inconsistency, so any change in the PID's synergy bias B_syn is a change of type, not of amount. In 200 \|Gaussian\| TPMs the macroscale gained B_syn by about 0.005–0.07; in 185 near-deterministic ones most with macro B_syn < 0.5 lost it. One redundancy function, no robustness check, tiny constructed systems. The "unifying theory" of the title is a framing: the EI section re-describes a known decomposition and adds no result. | Active |
| [THEORY-582](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-582.md) | Causal coupling between a process and something outside it does not by itself make that thing part of the process, so an argument from coupling to extended cognition needs a further premise saying what makes a process cognitive | Adams & Aizawa (2001), [LIT-438](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-438.md), read in [NOTE-368](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-368.md), and their reply to Clark (2010, read from a draft), [LIT-455](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-455.md), read in [NOTE-380](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-380.md). A thermostat's bimetallic strip, the kidney's filtration and a nerve at a neuromuscular junction are each coupled to more than themselves, and their processes do not extend. The 2010 text names the inference the "coupling-constitution fallacy". The point is that coupling does not entail parthood. It is not shown that coupling never accompanies parthood, nor that the extended-mind authors relied on coupling alone. | Active |
| [THEORY-584](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-584.md) | The quantum fidelity tr√(ρ1^{1/2}ρ0ρ1^{1/2}) is exactly the classical Bhattacharyya overlap of the two states' outcome distributions minimized over all measurements, and the minimum is attained by a projective measurement whose eigenvalues are square roots of likelihood ratios | Fuchs (1995), [LIT-018](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-018.md), read in full in [NOTE-021](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-021.md). min over POVMs of Σ_b √(tr ρ0E_b)√(tr ρ1E_b) equals tr√(ρ1^{1/2}ρ0ρ1^{1/2}) (Eq. 3.28), attained in the eigenbasis of M = ρ1^{-1/2}√(ρ1^{1/2}ρ0ρ1^{1/2})ρ1^{-1/2} (Eq. 3.67), whose eigenvalues are √(tr ρ0E_b / tr ρ1E_b) (Eq. 3.92). Proved for invertible ρ1 with a separate support construction, in finite dimension. The fidelity is the unsquared one; Jozsa's is its square. The thesis says nothing about trace distance, and the analogous problems for Rényi overlaps and the quantum Chernoff bound are left open. | Active |
| [THEORY-585](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-585.md) v2 | In the Döring–Isham scheme for realising collections of systems in topoi, disjoint sums of quantum systems compose exactly; along a tensor product of finite-dimensional systems, the pull-back of a constituent's quantity agrees with the composite's own quantity at a context exactly when every projection in it with proper support on the first factor has the form P⊗1, so it fails for every non-scalar quantity and no operator on the composite realises the pull-back | Döring & Isham, paper IV (2007/8), [LIT-310](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-310.md) ([NOTE-285](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-285.md)), restated in [LIT-378](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-378.md) §§11–13 ([NOTE-326](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-326.md)). Classical physics satisfies the translation condition (3.18) exactly. For quantum disjoint sums the pull-back of δ̆(A₁⊕A₂) is δ̆(A₁) (Lemma 4.2, 4.24; checked). For H₁⊗H₂ the pull-back gives δ(Â₁)_{V_W}⊗1̂ at each context W, which equals δ(Â₁⊗1̂)_W on contexts V₁⊗ℂ1̂. That it differs elsewhere, and that no operator realises it, are asserted. The rules are "partly experimental", and the trivial-system rule contradicts the series' own definition of contexts. | Active |
| [THEORY-587](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-587.md) | A U-turn stopping rule for Hamiltonian Monte Carlo leaves the target invariant once the trajectory is built as a random balanced doubling tree and the next state is drawn only from states that could have regenerated it; with a dual-averaged step size it matched the best hand-tuned identity-mass HMC on two of four test posteriors and beat it about threefold on the other two, and its ergodicity is not shown | Hoffman & Gelman (2011), [LIT-085](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-085.md), read in full in [NOTE-081](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-081.md). The invariance argument (conditions C.1–C.4 and the 2⁻ʲ tree probability) is complete, and so is the O(j)-memory kernel. Ergodicity is not addressed. The efficiency comparison is against HMC with an identity mass matrix on four smooth, near-unimodal targets, and the dual-averaging constants were tuned on one of the four. The account is of the 2011 algorithm; production NUTS has since changed its selection rule, U-turn criterion and adaptation. | Active |
| [THEORY-592](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-592.md) | Every unital Banach *-algebra satisfying Gelfand and Naimark's norm conditions is isometrically *-isomorphic to a norm-closed algebra of operators on a Hilbert space, built from positive functionals by what is now the GNS construction, and a commutative one is the algebra of all continuous functions on its compact maximal-ideal space | Gelfand & Naimark (1943), [LIT-313](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-313.md), read in full in [NOTE-303](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-303.md). Theorem 1 embeds every normed *-ring in B(H) for a Hilbert space not assumed separable; Lemma 1 is the commutative case, resting on Gelfand's 1941 paper and Šilov's boundary. The paper never says "C*-algebra" or "GNS". It assumes two axioms it suspected redundant, and notes that a single norm identity may replace two others. It gives the object-level isomorphism R ≅ C(𝔐), not a categorical duality, and nothing on uniqueness or irreducibility of the representation. | Active |
| [THEORY-595](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-595.md) | A filter over a set of worlds is a finitely consistent propositional theory and an ultrafilter a negation-complete one; read so, the ultrafilter extension theorem is Lindenbaum's lemma for propositions, and Łoś's theorem builds a model that makes true exactly what an ultrafilter says, which proves first-order compactness without proof theory, given the axiom of choice | Turner (preprint 2021, published 2025), [LIT-145](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-145.md), read in [NOTE-177](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-177.md). An expository paper: "None of the results are novel" (p. 2). Maximal, prime and ultra filters coincide (Thm 2); every filter extends to an ultrafilter (Thm 3); Łoś's theorem (Thm 9); compactness (Thm 12). The results are standard and correct, though the write-up has slips. A filter is only finitely consistent, and that is the point. The pairings with Lindenbaum and Henkin are analogies, not reductions. | Active |
| [THEORY-597](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-597.md) | Meditation-related experiences that Western Buddhist practitioners report as challenging span 59 kinds in seven domains, from fear and sleep change to altered self-other boundaries, and they are reported in daily practice, at under an hour a day and in the first days of practice, not only on intensive retreat; the frequencies come from a sample chosen for difficulty, and the causal link is the practitioners' own attribution | Lindahl, Fisher, Cooper, Rosen & Britton (2017), [LIT-066](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-066.md), read in full in [NOTE-036](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-036.md). Interviews with 60 Western Buddhist practitioners, recruited for having had a challenging meditation-related experience, and 32 teachers and clinicians were coded into 59 experience categories in seven domains. Some practitioners reported onset within ten days of starting, at under an hour a day, or in daily practice. That rebuts the claim that difficulties arise only on retreat or in the predisposed. It gives no rates and no relative risk: the sample was chosen for difficulty, and causation is self-attributed, with a causality score of 2 or more built into inclusion. | Active |
| [THEORY-598](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-598.md) | Group interactions that enter a dynamical model linearly, as in diffusion on simplices or random walks on hypergraphs with edge-independent vertex weights, reduce to pairwise dynamics on a reweighted graph; the abrupt transitions, bistability and stabilised coexistence reported for higher-order systems come from group terms that enter nonlinearly, and whether the representation is a hypergraph or a simplicial complex is itself a modelling claim that changes the outcome | Battiston et al. (2020), [LIT-091](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-091.md), read in full in [NOTE-057](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-057.md). A review: the reduction results are its own §V algebra (three-body linear diffusion becomes a weighted graph Laplacian, Eq. 35) and reported results it cites (Chitra and Raphael on hypergraph walks); the nonlinear effects are one-paper summaries, mostly mean-field or all-to-all. The review never states the condition as a result, and its introduction and conclusion claim more ("no doubts", "profoundly change"), citing linear cases among the examples. The condition is the record's reading of what its body shows; edge-dependent vertex weights also escape the reduction. | Active |
| [THEORY-599](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-599.md) | In trained neural-network weights stored as BF16 or FP32, nearly all the redundancy a lossless coder can remove lies in the floating-point exponent, which occupies about 40 of its 256 values and compresses to about a third under single-symbol Huffman coding, while sign and mantissa are near-incompressible; the redundancy belongs to the number format, not to the learned function | Hershcovitch et al. (2024), ZipNN, [LIT-268](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-268.md), read in full in [NOTE-241](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-241.md). Fifteen models broken down by byte group (Table II), with the exponent skew shown on four (Fig. 2) from 1 GB middle slices. A parameter shuffle changes Zstd's exponent compression by at most 0.05%, so the gain is order-0. The paper never computes an entropy. Its explanation of the skew is partly wrong as stated, and its remark that the redundancy shows overparametrization unused does not follow from what it measured. | Active |
| [THEORY-601](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-601.md) | Among US undergraduates in the HERI surveys, students with higher verbal ability and stronger self-reported intellectual dispositions select into philosophy, and after adjusting for their entering SAT or freshman scores philosophy majors still score higher than other majors on GRE Verbal (SMD 0.48) and LSAT (0.35) but not on GRE Quantitative, and report more Habits of Mind and Pluralistic Orientation; the adjusted advantage is an association, not a shown effect of studying philosophy | Prinzing & Vazquez (2025), [LIT-155](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-155.md), read in full in [NOTE-167](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-167.md). HERI/CIRP freshman–senior data on 649,511 students at 804 institutions, 4,843 philosophy majors. Selection is real (SAT Verbal OR 1.57, SAT Math none). Baseline-adjusted mixed models and an IPTW check agree on the verbal and logical-test advantage and on its absence for quantitative tests. All test scores are self-reported, the SAT is an imperfect baseline for the LSAT, and nothing rules out faster verbal growth or harder test preparation among those who choose philosophy, so the paper's causal title is not part of this account. | Active |
| [THEORY-602](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-602.md) | An ergodic source's entropy is the least average rate at which it can be encoded, a noisy channel has a capacity below which any rate can be sent with arbitrarily small error and above which the equivocation cannot fall below the excess, and a source can be reproduced at a given fidelity over a channel exactly when its rate for that fidelity does not exceed the capacity; Shannon rests the justification of entropy on these theorems, not on the axioms that single out −Σ p log p | Shannon (1948), [LIT-764](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-764.md), read in [NOTE-591](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-591.md): Parts I–II closely, Parts III–V and the later appendices skimmed for their theorem statements. The noisy-channel achievability proof is a random-coding sketch at the typical-set level, not a full ε–δ argument, and the strong converse is not proved; the theorems themselves were later made rigorous. Shannon says the uniqueness theorem for H is "in no way necessary" to the theory. The theorems assume ergodic, finite-state sources and channels and say nothing about meaning. | Active |
| [THEORY-603](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-603.md) | In the Iowa gambling task, every one of ten controls and none of six patients with bilateral ventromedial prefrontal damage developed anticipatory skin-conductance responses, and three patients who could state the right strategy still did not switch to the good decks; the controls' preference for the good decks became significant only once they reported a hunch, so the study does not show advantageous choice or deck-specific bodily signals before any awareness | Bechara, Damasio, Tranel & Damasio (1997), [LIT-383](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-383.md), read in [NOTE-331](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-331.md). The robust results are the group difference in anticipatory SCRs (Fisher's exact, one-sided P < 0.001) and the insufficiency of stated knowledge in three patients. The abstract's "before they realized which strategy worked best" and "before they knew" outrun notes 8 and 9: the pre-hunch choice preference was not significant, and the pre-hunch SCR effect reported is group × period, with no bad-versus-good deck test. Nothing here shows that the SCR, or what it indexes, causes the choice. | Active |
| [THEORY-605](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-605.md) | In any ontological model that reproduces the quantum predictions and treats independently prepared systems as having product distributions over a joint state that is just the list of their states, distinct pure quantum states have distributions over the ontic state whose supports overlap in measure zero, so the pure state is fixed by the ontic state; approximate agreement within ε bounds the overlap by 2ε^{1/n} | Pusey, Barrett & Rudolph (2011), [LIT-062](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-062.md), read in full in [NOTE-030](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-030.md). For any two non-orthogonal pure states, n copies prepared independently and an entangled measurement in which each outcome is impossible for one product preparation force zero overlap; with ε error, D(µ0, µ1) ≥ 1 − 2ε^{1/n} (Eq. 7). Determinism and locality are not assumed. Preparation independence, in its strong product-space form, carries the weight, and dropping it permits ψ-epistemic models. The theorem excludes overlap, not every reading of ψ as knowledge, and it does not reach theories outside the ontological-models framework. | Active |
| [THEORY-608](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-608.md) | On one physical piano-movers puzzle scaled to the solver, ant groups solve better as they grow, while human groups barred from speech and gesture solve worse than individuals and talking groups only about as well as one; large ant groups keep speed and heading through wall contact, and the human mechanisms offered are fitted or observed informally, not tested | Dreyer et al. (2024), [LIT-075](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-075.md), read in [NOTE-040](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-040.md). Large ant groups (n = 28) reach about 90–100% success by 400 corridor widths, small groups (n = 48) about 50%. Restricted human groups do 32% worse than individuals' median, talking groups 7% better. There are no inferential statistics. The ant persistence mechanism is supported by collision data and a model whose carrier numbers fall short of calibration; the human majority vote (greediness P = 0.2) is tuned by eye, and "follow a random leader" rests on unrecorded observation. One ant species, one puzzle, one human population. | Active |
| [THEORY-609](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-609.md) | When implementing an automaton requires reliable, counterfactual-supporting transitions for every formal state, Putnam's construction fails, but any system with a clock and a dial still implements every inputless finite-state automaton, and any system with the right input–output dependencies, an input memory and a dial implements every finite-state automaton with those dependencies, so finite-state automata cannot carry computational sufficiency; combinatorial-state automata are argued, not proved, to escape | Chalmers (1996), [LIT-404](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-404.md), read in [NOTE-342](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-342.md) from the author's HTML copy. The failure of Putnam's construction and the clock-and-dial and input-memory theorems are constructive proofs given the definitions, so FSA-functionalism "still almost reduces to behaviorism". That a combinatorial-state automaton can be implemented only by the right fine-grained causal structure is a sketch: the obvious blind construction grows by a factor of n per step, and that every construction does is asserted. Logically possible false implementations and the one-region-per-component condition are left open by the author. | Active |
| [THEORY-611](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-611.md) | Classifier-free guidance extrapolates between a conditional and an unconditional score learned by one network; with exact scores this equals classifier guidance by the classifier the generative model defines through Bayes' rule, but learned scores need not be conservative, so the guided field is in general the gradient of no density and the tilted distribution that motivates guidance is not shown to be what is sampled | Ho & Salimans (2022), [LIT-839](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-839.md), read in full in [NOTE-603](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-603.md), with the derivations of Section 3 checked line by line. The non-conservativeness argument is credited to Salimans & Ho (2021). The FID–IS trade-off is shown on class-conditional ImageNet only. [NOTE-603](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-603.md) declined a THEORY because the anthology holds the account of what the guidance weight does to metrics; this one states only the probabilistic point, which the record's [CLAIM-123](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-123.md) uses. | Active |
| [THEORY-617](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-617.md) | In additive Gaussian noise independent of an input of finite power whose law does not depend on the signal-to-noise ratio, the derivative of mutual information with respect to that ratio is half the minimum mean-square error of the optimal noncausal estimator, so mutual information is accumulated estimation error over SNR; in continuous time the causal filtering error equals the noncausal error averaged over SNR, and the identity fails with feedback | Guo, Shamai & Verdú (2004), [LIT-058](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-058.md), read in full in [NOTE-086](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-086.md). Proved five ways for every finite-power input, in scalar, vector, discrete-time and continuous-time forms. It concerns the optimal, conditional-mean estimator; carrying it to a trained diffusion model's learned denoiser needs the mismatched version, which is later work. Theorems 3, 4 and 11 are stated without proof. | Active |
| [THEORY-619](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-619.md) | Over the poset of commutative von Neumann subalgebras, coarse-graining a projector to a smaller subalgebra is exactly the direct image of its clopen region of the Gelfand spectrum under restriction, so the coarse-graining presheaf is the presheaf of clopen spectral regions; and a quantum state's sieve-valued truth values are fixed by one coherent family of regions, its supports: a proposition is true at a subcontext exactly when the support there lies under the coarse-grained proposition | Butterfield & Isham (2001), "Topos Perspective on the Kochen-Specker Theorem: IV", [LIT-382](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-382.md), read in full in [NOTE-328](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-328.md). §2.4 proves G ≅ CloΣ: restricting the characters of V₁ that make P̂ true gives exactly the characters of V₂ that make its coarse-graining true, via a cited state-extension theorem. Theorem 3.1 shows that any assignment defined by "support ≤ coarse-grained proposition", with supports forming a global element of G, is a sieve-valued valuation obeying FUNC; a state's supports qualify. Both theorems are close to definitional. Nothing here builds Heyting operations on clopen sub-objects. | Active |
| [THEORY-620](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-620.md) | Walsh's 1923 functions are a closed orthonormal set on (0, 1) of ±1-valued step functions, each a parity of finitely many binary digits, whose expansions behave like Fourier series: grouped uniform convergence for continuous functions, convergence under bounded variation, localisation, Cesàro summability, and divergence at any chosen point for some continuous function | Walsh (1923), [LIT-300](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-300.md), read in full in [NOTE-281](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-281.md), with the explicit formula and the Lebesgue-constant recurrence checked for small n. Closure is inherited from Haar's system, to which Walsh's is related by an orthogonal change of basis within each dyadic level. Theorems II–X give the Fourier-like convergence theory. The paper never mentions groups or characters: that these functions are the characters of the Cantor group, and of the Boolean cube on n digits, is a later identification. | Active |
| [THEORY-623](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-623.md) | In the two tests of contextuality in language data that the record has read, the contextuality is put there by the experimenter or not secured: meaning-selection models of ambiguous phrases estimated from corpora are all signalling and their two Contextuality-by-Default verdicts are plausibly noncontextual by their own bootstrap, while BERT's 52 million anaphora models have a support fixed by the sentence schema, so whether each counts as contextual depends only on how uncertain the model's three referent choices are | Lo, Sadrzadeh & Mansfield (2024), [LIT-844](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-844.md), read in [NOTE-648](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-648.md), and Wang, Sadrzadeh, Abramsky & Cervantes (2021), [LIT-842](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-842.md), read in [NOTE-645](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-645.md). Both readings recomputed the criteria. That 71.1% CbD-contextual measures BERT's uncertainty is [NOTE-648](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-648.md)'s derivation from the stipulated support (CNT1 = 2 − Δ). The only possibilistically contextual phrase model has hand-set supports. Neither study uses human judgements, so neither bears on whether people's interpretations are contextual. | Active |
| [THEORY-629](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-629.md) | Every continuous linear functional on a Hilbert space is the inner product with a unique vector of the same norm, given in any orthonormal basis by the conjugated values of the functional on the basis; completeness is what makes it so, and Riesz's 1907 statement on L² asserted only that a representing function exists | Adler (2021), [LIT-243](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-243.md), read in full in [NOTE-854](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-854.md): two complete proofs, by projection (Thm 3.5) and by an orthonormal basis (Thm 4.9), with completeness used once, in the projection theorem. Riesz (1907), [LIT-326](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-326.md), read in [NOTE-289](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-289.md), is the priority note: existence of k with U(f) = ∫ f k for continuous linear U on square-summable functions, stated without proof, uniqueness or norm. The theorem says nothing about kernels, factorisation or uniqueness of representations. Both readings advise citing a textbook for anything leaned on. | Active |
| [THEORY-632](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-632.md) | Purity is moralized in self-report: in morality-as-cooperation's own questionnaire studies, purity items are rated about as morally relevant as loyalty and authority items, and harmless purity violations are condemned, so that theory's prediction that non-cooperative behaviour is morally neutral fails unless purity is itself cooperative | Curry, Jones Chesters & Van Lissa (2019), [LIT-496](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-496.md), read in [NOTE-412](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-412.md), against the prediction stated in Curry (2016), [LIT-503](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-503.md) ([NOTE-408](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-408.md)), with the harmless-wrongs studies Haidt (2001) reports, [LIT-511](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-511.md) ([NOTE-403](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-403.md)). In two samples, MFQ purity items are rated morally relevant at the level of ingroup and authority items, and the authors concede this "appear[s] to contradict" the theory. It is self-report from people asked about purity, not a blind count of what societies moralize, and it does not say whether purity is cooperative. | Active |
| [THEORY-634](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-634.md) | In a ring of M chemotactic catalyst species, each making the next one's substrate, the non-reciprocal nearest-neighbour coupling makes the linear stability matrix circulant: the uniform state goes unstable for any M exactly when the species attract themselves, and the parity of M then decides the leading mode, a real alternating mode for even M that sorts species by parity into two static clusters, and a complex pair for odd M that can give persistent oscillation | Ouazan-Reboul, Agudo-Canalejo & Golestanian (2023), [LIT-036](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-036.md), read in [NOTE-079](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-079.md). The spectrum is exact for equal parameters (Eq. 5): instability iff μ(p) − μ(s) < 0, real leading eigenvalue for M = 2K, complex pair for M = 2K + 1. Brownian dynamics at M = 5 and 6 bear out the linear predictions; the odd-cycle oscillation is one trajectory at one parameter set. Direct metabolic partners repel; same-parity second neighbours co-aggregate. The origin-of-life reading is untested, and the authors concede in the review file that real catalysts' mobilities are unknown. | Active |
| [THEORY-635](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-635.md) | If the quantum state of a Bohmian system is identified with the velocity dispositions it induces on the particles, inequivalent states can share one dispositional history: every energy eigenstate of a free particle in a box induces zero velocity everywhere, so the reading erases differences of energy and of typicality unless the map from states to velocity fields is injective for generic solutions, which is conjectured, not proved | Belot (2011), [LIT-100](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-100.md), read in full in [NOTE-110](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-110.md). Under the guidance law ψ(t) gives a vector field X_t on configuration space, read as a holistic disposition. For a particle in [0,1], each φn(x) = sin(πnx) gives zero velocity everywhere, so infinitely many energy eigenstates share one dispositional history, and the distinction between φ1 and φ2 in energy and typicality is lost. The rescue rests on Goldstein's unproved genericity conjecture (fn. 41), and the problem arises only for closed systems (fn. 42). It is a counterexample to one reading, not a verdict on ψ's category. | Active |
| [THEORY-636](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-636.md) | In vignette studies of US online participants, judgements that an outcome happened because the agent wanted it move with judgements that it was done intentionally when luck is manipulated, and predict them better than know-how or probability-raising do; but they account for only about half of the luck effect, and in one morally neutral case the two come apart | Quillien (2026), [LIT-132](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-132.md), read in [NOTE-092](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-092.md). Three Prolific studies (N = 198, 673, 142; ratings 1–7). Causation is the strongest predictor of intentionality (standardized β .46, .56, .53, against know-how .33, .20, .27 and probability-raising .14, .16, .10), and a pre-registered Knowledge × Process interaction predicted by the causal account holds (F(1, 423) = 32). The evidence is correlational, the mediation exploratory and partial (64%, 45%, 49%), and in the neutral Kraemer vignette causation shows no effect where intentionality does. The "model" is verbal; robustness is never measured. | Active |
| [THEORY-639](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-639.md) | Inductive risk arises not only when a hypothesis is accepted but in choosing a significance level, in characterising data and in interpreting results: in the dioxin cancer studies each of these choices traded false positives against false negatives, three panels scored the same rat-liver slides differently, and threshold and no-threshold readings of the same data underlie regulatory limits about 100 times apart | Douglas (2000), [LIT-139](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-139.md), read in [NOTE-145](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-145.md). Three worked cases from one domain, dioxin toxicology and its regulation, on secondary data (EPA 1994; Kociba et al. 1978; Goodman & Sauer 1992). The structural point and the variation in slide scoring are strongly supported. The 100-fold figure is cited from Finkel (1988) and Greenlee et al. (1991). This is the descriptive half of the paper; the claim that values are therefore required is [THEORY-442](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-442.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-640](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-640.md) | Measured as mutual 10-nearest-neighbour overlap, competent vision models agree more with one another and better language models agree more with vision models, but the cross-modal score reaches only 0.16 of a possible 1, is the maximum over all layer pairs, and was adopted after a global kernel metric showed only a very weak trend | Huh, Cheung, Wang & Isola (2024), [LIT-302](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-302.md), read in [NOTE-286](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-286.md). Across 78 vision models, those solving more VTAB tasks agree more in mutual k-nearest-neighbour structure; language models with lower bits-per-byte agree more with vision models on 1,024 image–caption pairs. The cross-modal score "only reaches 0.16" of 1, is maximised over layer pairs, and the metric was chosen after CKA "revealed a very weak trend". It is local neighbourhood agreement that rises with competence, not kernel equality and not convergence to a model of reality. | Active |
| [THEORY-641](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-641.md) v2 | Under a well-specified, identifiable parametric Markov model of the target given the joint past, with ergodic lagged states, transfer entropy is the limit of the normalised log-likelihood ratio for the null of no dependence on the source's past, so it is Granger-sense predictive improvement; for finite-state chains the plug-in estimator is exactly that statistic, and under the null and the usual regularity it is asymptotically χ² with the difference in parameter counts as degrees of freedom | Barnett & Bossomaier (2012), [LIT-048](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-048.md), read in full in [NOTE-053](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-053.md). The consistency result is a one-line consequence of Props. 1–2, and Prop. 2 is argued informally. The χ² null is imported from Wald (1943), whose regularity conditions are not checked. The non-central χ² for T > 0 is at best a local-alternative approximation. The finite-state identity and the Gaussian equivalence (half the Granger statistic) are exact. | Active |
| [THEORY-642](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-642.md) | Basic two-level type theory, an inner homotopy type theory with an outer level of strict equality, is conservative over homotopy type theory, so an inner type it proves inhabited is already inhabited in HoTT, but a fibrant-replacement type former would force uniqueness of identity proofs on the inner level | Annenkov, Capriotti, Kraus & Sattler (2017; MSCS 2023), [LIT-095](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-095.md), whose §§1–3 were read in full in [NOTE-047](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-047.md), the reading of the nLab page it supersedes ([LIT-040](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-040.md)). Props 2.18–2.19 prove that inhabitation of inner types is reflected, through a presheaf model over any model of HoTT. Thm 2.20 proves that a fibrant-replacement former implies UIP for inner types. The conservativity is the weak, inhabitation-reflecting kind. Results that use the axioms relating the two levels' natural numbers, which untruncated semisimplicial types need, are not known to transfer. | Active |
| [THEORY-645](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-645.md) | A countable discrete abelian group and a compact second-countable abelian group can each be recovered as the character group of the other, and a locally compact, connected, second-countable abelian group is a compact group plus ℝʳ; Pontryagin's 1934 paper does not prove duality for general locally compact abelian groups | Pontryagin (1934), [LIT-333](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-333.md), read in full in [NOTE-284](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-284.md). Theorem 5 and the First Fundamental Theorem give the duality between countable discrete and compact second-countable abelian groups, with characters valued in ℝ/ℤ. The compact half rests on Peter–Weyl with Haar measure, used to extract one-dimensional characters. The Second and Third Fundamental Theorems are structure theorems, not duality. Commutative only; for non-abelian groups the relevant object is Peter–Weyl, and characters are traces, not homomorphisms. General locally compact duality is van Kampen's (1935). | Active |
| [THEORY-649](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-649.md) | When agents holding uniformly random consistent theories over two or three atomic sentences each average their theories once, bit by bit, with all peers within a Hamming bound of confidence, an individual agent ends up with the inconsistent theory at most 1.81% of the time, but the chance that some agent in the group does reaches 6.4% for two sentences and 16.9% for three | Wenmackers (2011), [LIT-163](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-163.md), chapter 5, read in [NOTE-139](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-139.md). An exact count, extended by sampling, of how often one round of bounded-confidence averaging over theories yields the inconsistent theory. The per-agent fraction F_AG peaks at 1.8112% (M = 2) and 0.3215% (M = 3); the per-profile fraction F_OP reaches 6.4298% and 16.867%. The thesis's headline, that the risk "can be made arbitrarily small" by adding sentences, rests on two values of M and is contradicted for F_OP. | Active |
| [THEORY-652](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-652.md) | Over any field, a finite-dimensional associative algebra with no nilpotent two-sided ideal is uniquely a direct sum of simple algebras, and each simple algebra is a full matrix algebra over a division algebra, which over the reals can be the complex numbers or the quaternions | Wedderburn (1908), [LIT-309](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-309.md), read in full in [NOTE-280](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-280.md). Thm 17 with Thm 10 gives the unique decomposition into simple algebras; Thms 20–22 build n² matrix units from primitive idempotents and give simple = primitive × full matrix algebra. Primitive here means one idempotent, which makes the factor a division algebra once semisimple (Thm 15). The field is arbitrary, which was the paper's novelty. That the centre is spanned by the block identities follows from Thm 23's corollary; the paper never says "centre". The general splitting of an algebra into nilpotent plus semisimple parts is claimed in the summary but proved only in special cases. | Active |
| [THEORY-653](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-653.md) | In the ethnographic record of the 60-society HRAF Probability Sample, seven cooperative behaviours are described as good in 961 of 962 valenced mentions, but each is recorded in between 90% and 15% of the societies, and the coding could barely have registered a negative | Curry, Mullins & Whitehouse (2019), [LIT-047](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-047.md), read in [NOTE-034](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-034.md). Coding eHRAF paragraphs on the 60 Probability Sample societies found 962 morally valenced mentions of helping kin, helping one's group, reciprocating, bravery, deference, dividing disputed resources and respecting possession; 961 were positive. Presence ran from property (54/60) to fairness (9/60) and tracked ethnographic coverage (r = .43). The behaviours are defined in virtue terms and conflicts were set aside, so a negative was nearly impossible to code. It is a description of the coded record, not a test of whether morality is only about cooperation. | Active |
| [THEORY-654](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-654.md) | For full-state linear-quadratic regulation of a single-input plant, the return-difference identity keeps the sensitivity at or below 1 at every frequency, so the loop tolerates any gain increase, a gain cut to one half and at least 60° of phase error for any Q ≥ 0 and r > 0; the guarantee does not carry over when the state is replaced by an observer's estimate | Başar, Meyn & Perkins (2020), [LIT-051](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-051.md), graduate course notes read in full in [NOTE-062](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-062.md), with every worked example recomputed. §10.6 derives \|1 + L(jω)\|² = 1 + \|P(jω)\|²/r ≥ 1 for the full-state loop, hence \|S\| ≤ 1 and the classical margins. The derivation is for one input; the multi-input version needs more, which the notes do not discuss. The Pendubot thread shows a controllable, observable plant whose one-sensor observer-based design has gain margin below 10⁻². The result is Kalman's and standard; the notes are an adequate free citation for it. | Active |
| [THEORY-659](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-659.md) | In the EEAS's 2024 sample of 505 foreign information manipulation incidents, the overt state voice is a small core: of the 2,055 channels that recur across incidents, 20% are attributed to Russia, 3.5% to China and 76.5% are not attributed, after some 28,000 disposable inauthentic accounts are set aside; the sample is not representative, and the four-tier Exposure Matrix used to grade channels' ties to a state is unvalidated | European External Action Service (2025), [LIT-084](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-084.md), the 3rd EEAS report on FIMI threats, read in [NOTE-060](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-060.md). A description of what the EEAS monitored, which the report itself says is not a basis for general trends. The 76.5% is a share of a filtered co-involvement graph, not of the 38,000 channels, though the report's conclusions restate it as such. The Exposure Matrix grades attribution in four tiers by evidence and treats it as revisable; no inter-rater test or worked classification is given, and the strongest evidence is proprietary or classified. | Active |
| [THEORY-661](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-661.md) | In a nearly decomposable system, where interactions within subsystems are much stronger than interactions between them, each subsystem's short-run behaviour is approximately independent of the others', and in the long run each depends on the others only through their aggregate behaviour; so a hierarchy defined by intensity of interaction separates fast dynamics inside its parts from slow, aggregate dynamics between them | Simon (1962), [LIT-905](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-905.md), read in full in [NOTE-704](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-704.md). The two propositions are a theorem of Simon & Ando (1961), cited and not reproduced, and established since. Simon widens hierarchy to any nesting of interrelated subsystems, with or without authority, identified by who interacts with whom. His claims that social systems are prominently nearly decomposable, and that higher organisational levels run slower, are assertion and "probably true". The watchmaker argument is a model whose numbers he says not to take seriously. | Active |
| [THEORY-664](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-664.md) | In a finite-dimensional probabilistic theory with unrestricted effects and local tomography, if every system can steer each of its own states from a composite with a copy of itself, every irreducible state space is homogeneous and weakly self-dual; steering does not yet give strong self-duality, so it stops short of the Jordan-algebraic and quantum state spaces | Barnum, Gaebler & Wilce (2009), [LIT-081](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-081.md), read in full in [NOTE-082](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-082.md). A bipartite state steers its marginal iff its map on effects is a strong quotient of order intervals (Thm 5.4). With matching dimensions a steering state is an order-isomorphism, and a cone is homogeneous iff every interior state purifies to an isomorphism state (Thm 4.1). Hence universal self-steering gives homogeneity and weak self-duality (Prop. 5.8). The weaker Prop. 5.7 is thinly argued. The C*-algebraic conclusion of §6 needs strong self-duality, which the paper assumes rather than derives. | Active |
| [THEORY-668](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-668.md) | When the encoder is restricted to prunings of one fixed hierarchy of nested partitions, any non-negatively weighted sum of relevant information, irrelevant information and compression decomposes into per-node terms, so a bottom-up recursion finds the unique optimal tree with fewest leaves exactly in linear time, while greedy top-down splitting can miss information lying below a level that carries none; penalising irrelevant information only prunes the information-bottleneck tree | Larsson, Maity & Tsiotras (2022), [LIT-868](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-868.md), read in full in [NOTE-676](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-676.md), every proof followed step by step. The decomposition is the chain rule for refinements, and the recursion is the classic bottom-up pruning of a fixed tree. [NOTE-676](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-676.md) declined a THEORY as exact but narrow; it is filed because the reading supports it as stated and its greedy-failure point bears on how hierarchy is measured. The hierarchy is given, not found, and the evaluation is one image. | Active |
| [THEORY-672](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-672.md) | In the iterated Prisoner's Dilemma with a probability w of meeting again, no strategy does better against an established TIT FOR TAT than TIT FOR TAT does against itself if and only if w ≥ (T−R)/(T−P) and w ≥ (T−R)/(R−S); always defecting is stable for every w, a cluster of reciprocators can invade it, and a nice stable strategy resists clusters, but the stability is only neutral, since always cooperating ties | Axelrod & Hamilton (1981), [LIT-498](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-498.md), read in full in [NOTE-411](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-411.md). Against TIT FOR TAT the best reply is always-defect or alternation, which gives the condition on w. The cluster result and the "ratchet" are explicit payoff comparisons. "Evolutionarily stable" here means no mutant does better, which is weaker than Maynard Smith and Price's definition: always cooperate does exactly as well. The model is deterministic and error-free. Tournament robustness is a separate, empirical claim about the strategies people submitted. | Active |
| [THEORY-676](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-676.md) | Dewar's information-theoretic derivation of maximum entropy production does not reach the far-from-equilibrium regime where the principle is applied: the 2003 route needs a mean-field step and an unargued assumption about path counts, the 2005 route's orthogonality condition, which yields both maximum and minimum dissipation, holds only with linear constitutive relations, and the 2003 self-organized-criticality corollary is an artefact of a quadratic expansion | Grinstein & Linsker (2007), [LIT-525](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-525.md), read in [NOTE-422](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-422.md), against Dewar (2003), [LIT-521](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-521.md), read in [NOTE-426](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-426.md). The self-organized-criticality point was checked against Dewar 2003 and is correct. The linearity point concerns Dewar 2005, which the record could not read; it is held on the Comment's account of its equations and on an exactly solvable spin chain, re-derived. The Comment removes one derivation and one application. It does not say MEP is false, and it says the existence of far-from-equilibrium extremal principles "has not been settled". | Active |
| [THEORY-677](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-677.md) | Under uncertainty about which beings are sentient, an appeal to precaution does not by itself fix which error is worse to make: precaution on behalf of a possibly sentient being and precaution on behalf of human liberty point opposite ways, and judging which mistake costs more turns on the very science in doubt | Schwitzgebel & Sinnott-Armstrong (2026), [LIT-166](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-166.md), read in [NOTE-116](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-116.md) from the September 2025 draft. A conceptual argument with worked cases, which the reading rates strong: "By itself, an appeal to precaution does not specify the type of error most to be avoided" (p. 8). Birch's framework puts the burden on whoever risks harming a sentience candidate; Mill's harm principle, read as a precaution, puts it on whoever would restrict liberty. The record holds the point, not the reviewers' reading of Birch's books, which it has not read. | Active |
| [THEORY-679](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-679.md) | For dynamics obeying detailed balance in a heat bath, the heat released in a transition between observer-defined macrostates is bounded below by the log-odds against its reversal less the internal entropy change; where a replicator's likeliest way back is a copy decaying within one generation, the bound grows with the copy's durability and the speed of copying, not with the information copied | England (2012; J. Chem. Phys. 2013), [LIT-515](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-515.md), read in [NOTE-419](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-419.md). The general bound, β⟨ΔQ⟩ + ln π(II→I) + ΔS_int ≥ 0, is a coarse-grained second law and was re-derived. Applied to replication it gives a heat cost of about 2n ln(n τ_decay/τ_div) per copy, which falls away as division slows. The numbers for E. coli (within a factor of three of the bound) and RNA rest on an upper bound on the reverse probability that is argued from biology, not proved, and on an internal-entropy term set "arbitrarily". It prices finite-time irreversibility, not information, and draws no line between living and non-living replicators. | Active |
| [THEORY-683](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-683.md) | Permuting a fixed set of few-shot examples moves a GPT-family model's classification accuracy between near chance and near the supervised state of the art, at every model size tested; the good orders are specific to the model, the spread survives more examples and calibration, and bad orders mostly fail by predicting one label | Lu et al. (2021, ACL 2022), [LIT-833](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-833.md), read in [NOTE-626](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-626.md). All 24 orders of four balanced SST-2 examples give accuracies from about 50% to above 85%, in GPT-2 and GPT-3 models of eight sizes; Spearman correlations of order accuracy between sizes lie between −0.35 and 0.27 (175B against 2.7B: 0.05). The variance stays high up to 32 examples and after calibration. It is a measurement on causal GPT models and text classification, with the transfer analysis resting on one example set, and the paper finds no property of an order that predicts its effect. | Active |
| [THEORY-685](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-685.md) | The Mizohata–Takeuchi conjecture fails for every compact C² hypersurface with a point of non-zero curvature: for each large R a function and a weight violate it by a factor of order log R, which refutes Stein's conjecture as stated and closes the Mizohata–Takeuchi route to loss-free endpoint multilinear restriction | Cairo (2025), [LIT-030](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-030.md), read in full in [NOTE-051](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-051.md), which checked the counting and exponent bookkeeping. The paper states the theorem for any C² hypersurface not lying in a hyperplane; the proof needs a curved point, which a connected such surface has. The incidence lemma (§4) is the step a non-specialist could not verify. The loss is log R, not a power, and the counterexample is a family indexed by R. It does not refute endpoint multilinear restriction itself. Its proposed local replacement has since been refuted with power loss on a dense family of surfaces, per the abstract of a later paper. | Active |
| [THEORY-686](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-686.md) v2 | An observation modelled as a monotone map between preorders can show of a joined system more than the join of its observations of the parts, and out of a preorder with all joins the observations that preserve all joins, the empty join and infinite joins included, are exactly the left adjoints | Fong & Spivak (2018), [LIT-803](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-803.md), Chapter 1, read closely in a Skimmed NOTE ([NOTE-601](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-601.md)) whose other chapters were seen only at their openings. Def. 1.93, after Adam, defines a generative effect as Φ(a) ∨ Φ(b) < Φ(a ∨ b). Prop. 1.111 and Thm 1.115 give that left adjoints preserve all joins and, from a source with all joins, only they do. The results are standard order theory, re-derived by the record because NOTE-601 is a skim. The absence of generative effects is weaker than preserving all joins, and does not characterise the left adjoints. | Active |
| [THEORY-688](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-688.md) | In an actor-critic learner that can choose temporally extended options as well as primitive actions, options that fit the task speed learning, while options with ill-placed subgoals slow it, and options that fit an earlier layout keep the agent from finding a newly opened shortcut, so hierarchy helps only with the right subroutines | Botvinick, Niv and Barto (2009), [LIT-581](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-581.md), read in [NOTE-451](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-451.md). Toy simulations in a rooms domain with pre-trained options. Doorway options sped learning; window options slowed it; with a shortcut opened, primitive-only agents found the shortest path on 75% of runs while doorway-option agents never used it (mean 11.79 against 9.73 steps).
