It is a result about the model. That people or brains work this way is the separate, proposed account [THEORY-484](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-484.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-689](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-689.md) | A mobile robot built from parallel layers of simple finite-state machines, each linking sensing to action by itself and combined only by one layer suppressing or inhibiting another's signals, avoids obstacles, wanders and heads for distant places with no central world model, goal list or controller; shown at insect scale, on three layers of one physical robot | Brooks (1991, written 1987), [LIT-436](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-436.md), read in [NOTE-351](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-351.md). An existence proof by construction: the absence of central representation and control is true of the architecture by design, and the robot ran "for well over a year". The evidence is described, not measured; three layers ran on a robot and six in simulation. The claims that coherence exists only "in the eye of an observer", that representation is the wrong unit for most of intelligence, and that the method scales are assertion or labelled hypothesis. | Active |
| [THEORY-692](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-692.md) | Near equilibrium, steady states minimise entropy production and every fluctuation decays; far from it, the excess entropy production has no fixed sign, so a fluctuation can grow past an instability of the thermodynamic branch into a structure held up only by flows across the boundary, and thermodynamics supplies only a sufficient condition for such a state's stability, not a principle selecting which structure appears | Prigogine (1977), [LIT-516](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-516.md), read in full in [NOTE-424](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-424.md), with Cross & Hohenberg (1993), [LIT-527](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-527.md), skimmed in [NOTE-418](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-418.md). Minimum entropy production holds only for steady states in the strictly linear regime with constant coefficients. Beyond it, non-negative excess entropy production suffices for stability; its failure is not shown to give instability. Which structure appears is left to kinetics, boundaries and fluctuations. Cross and Hohenberg find no global minimisation principle beyond a perturbative one near threshold, and quote Glansdorff and Prigogine conceding that "the search for a universal kinetic potential has proved to be unsuccessful". | Active |
| [THEORY-695](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-695.md) | Two quantum states can be broadcast if and only if they commute, and cloned if and only if they are identical or orthogonal; the theorem is proved for invertible density operators and marks a line within quantum theory, not a witness of nonclassicality | Fuchs (1995), [LIT-018](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-018.md), §4.3, read in full in [NOTE-021](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-021.md), from the Barnum–Caves–Fuchs–Jozsa–Schumacher manuscript. Fidelity cannot decrease under partial trace or under the broadcasting map, so broadcasting forces equality conditions that make ρ0 commute with the optimal-fidelity operator. Proved for invertible ρ0, ρ1 only. Spekkens' epistricted classical theories ([LIT-007](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-007.md)) reproduce no-broadcasting, so the theorem states where broadcastability ends inside quantum theory and does not by itself certify nonclassicality. | Active |
| [THEORY-696](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-696.md) | Under multiplicative noise, members that pool their resources and split them equally every step each grow faster in the long run than they would alone, with no complementarity, relatedness or reciprocity: N independent geometric Brownian motions that share keep their drift μ and cut their volatility to σ/√N, raising each one's time-average growth rate from μ − σ²/2 to μ − σ²/(2N); the gain vanishes as their noise becomes perfectly correlated, and a sufficiently superior member does better alone | Peters & Adamou (2022), [LIT-035](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-035.md), read in [NOTE-059](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-059.md). The mathematics is correct and self-contained, and the paper's own citations show the pooled-variance result was known (McCloskey, Winterhalder, Uitdehaag, Kennedy et al.). Sharing leaves the ensemble rate μ unchanged, so an analysis built on expectations sees no reason to share, and the time average does. It holds with zero cost, perfect pooling, unbreakable pacts and unconstrained growth. It is a sufficient mechanism in that model, not a solution of the cooperation puzzle, and not a showing that cooperation is the default. | Active |
| [THEORY-697](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-697.md) | Sparse distributed memory's read weights each stored pattern by the number of hard locations within the read radius of both query and pattern, a ball-intersection count that falls roughly exponentially in Hamming distance over a local window, so softmax attention over cosine similarity of unit-norm queries and keys, with a fitted inverse temperature, approximates the SDM read there; the approximation cannot hold globally, since the binary count vanishes beyond twice the radius, and its inverse temperature comes from a regression, not from the paper's analytic bound | Bricken & Pehlevan (2021), [LIT-269](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-269.md), read in full in [NOTE-242](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-242.md), which re-evaluated the intersection formula and the fit. The exact intersection (Eq. 2) is checked against Kanerva's lune formula and simulation; eight SDM and fitted-softmax variants retrieve almost identically on random patterns, MNIST and CIFAR-10, with three named exceptions. The intersection is a staircase in distance, the fit holds to about dv = 20 for d = 15, the analytic β of App. B.2 is about 2–2.5 times too small, and every optimal radius assumes random patterns and addresses. The GPT-2 "confirmation" and the cerebellar implementation of attention are argument, not demonstration. | Active |
| [THEORY-698](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-698.md) | Thresholding linear attribute probes on a language model's embeddings yields a complete concept lattice for any incidence whatever, so the lattice is guaranteed by construction; what the Lattice Representation Hypothesis measured is per-attribute agreement with GPT-4o annotations at F1 70–83, and no lattice law | Xiong (2026), [LIT-267](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-267.md), read in [NOTE-240](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-240.md). Theorem 1 is the basic theorem of formal concept analysis applied to the crisp relation got by thresholding Fisher-LDA probes, and it holds for every binary relation; the paper's own proof plan says so. The empirical content is that the thresholded probes on three 7–8B models agree with a GPT-4o-annotated incidence at macro F1 69.7–83.2 and predict WordNet subsumption at F1 57.1–77.1. No closure, absorption or recovered-lattice comparison is tested, and the paper's join is not a lattice join as written. It is not evidence that language models encode a lattice beyond the incidence. | Active |
| [THEORY-700](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-700.md) | For jointly Gaussian stationary processes, Granger causality in Geweke's generalized-variance form is exactly twice the transfer entropy, conditional and multivariate, at the regressions' lags, because least-squares residual covariance is the partial covariance and a Gaussian's conditional entropy is half its log-determinant plus a constant | Barnett, Barrett & Seth (2009), [LIT-1171](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1171.md), read in full in [NOTE-934](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-934.md). F_{Y→X\|Z} = 2T_{Y→X\|Z}, exactly, for population quantities. The proof is two identities and was checked. Sample agreement depends on the entropy estimator. Both quantities are predictive; the authors keep them apart from physical causation. | Active |
| [THEORY-701](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-701.md) | Transfer entropy from J to I is the Kullback entropy of assuming that I's next state, given its last k states, does not depend on J's last l states, so it is zero exactly when J's past leaves I's transition law unchanged; unlike time-delayed mutual information it is directional and zero for static correlation, and it removes a common input only when that input is conditioned on | Schreiber (2000), [LIT-1177](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1177.md), read in full in [NOTE-940](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-940.md). The definition and its zero condition are exact. The comparison with delayed mutual information rests on two coupled-map lattices built with a known direction. The continuum-limit claim is asserted. The Letter's tent-map coefficient appears to be twice what Eq. 4 gives. | Active |
| [THEORY-702](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-702.md) | Transfer entropy is the average of a local transfer entropy, the log ratio at each observation of the destination's next-state probability with and without the source given the destination's past, which can be negative where the source misleads; the destination history must be long for it to exclude self-influence routed through the source; and conditioning also on the destination's other causal parents (complete) can differ sharply from conditioning on its past alone (apparent), as in elementary cellular automata, where long-history local transfer entropy picks out gliders and domain walls | Lizier, Prokopenko & Zomaya (2008), [LIT-1175](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1175.md), read in full in [NOTE-943](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-943.md). The local decomposition is an identity; the claims about k and about particles rest on elementary CAs judged by eye. Three worked local values and rule 18's XOR structure were checked. | Active |
| [THEORY-704](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-704.md) | In a stationary multivariate time series whose components include every relevant process, with interventions that are isolated exogenous changes and no instantaneous causation, a missing Granger-causal edge from a to b means intervening on a has no effect on b at the next step, non-ancestry means no effect at any horizon, and a set whose observed past blocks every back-door path into b's ancestors identifies the effect from observational data, as a multi-step linear-predictor coefficient in the Gaussian case | Eichler & Didelez (2007), [LIT-1164](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1164.md), read in full in [NOTE-941](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-941.md). The back-door results are proved; the edge-to-effect statements in the conclusion are said to follow by the same reasoning; the front-door proof is deferred. All conditions are sufficient, and Assumption 2.3 is untestable from observational data. Two worked effects were checked. | Active |
| [THEORY-705](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-705.md) v2 | For a target and two sources with finite alphabets, if unique information is to depend only on the two source–target pair marginals, then the minimum of the conditional mutual information over all joints with those marginals is an upper bound on every non-negative decomposition's unique information, and the shared and synergistic information it implies are lower bounds; this unique information vanishes exactly when the other source is Blackwell-sufficient, and the measures are non-negative, satisfy the bivariate partial-information axioms and the identity property, and do not extend to three sources on the partial-information lattice | Bertschinger et al. (2014), [LIT-1162](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1162.md), read in full in [NOTE-937](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-937.md). The bounds, the Blackwell characterisation and the properties are proved. The motivating property is argued, not derived. Example 30 and the Table 1 rows reproduce, except two entries that conflict with the paper's own Proposition 18. Under this measure, the record's transfer-entropy examples split exactly as under I_min. | Active |
| [THEORY-706](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-706.md) | Any redundancy function defined on the lattice of antichains of sources, ordered so that a collection precedes another when every source of the latter contains one of the former, has a Möbius inverse that decomposes the information a set of sources gives about a target into partial-information atoms summing to every subset's mutual information; for the I_min redundancy, the expected minimum specific information over sources, every atom is nonnegative, and interaction information is a signed mixture of atoms, synergy minus redundancy for three variables | Williams & Beer (2010), [LIT-1172](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1172.md), read in full in [NOTE-936](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-936.md). The lattice, the inversion and the nonnegativity proofs are exact and were followed; the lattice sizes and the 3-parity and three-copies cases were checked. What is not shown is that I_min measures shared information: it gives two independent copied bits 1 bit of redundancy (Harder, Salge and Polani). | Active |
| [THEORY-707](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-707.md) | Transfer entropy is not a measure of information flow, if flow means information in the target attributable solely to the source's past: as a conditional mutual information it equals the source's unique information plus its synergy with the target's past, so it can credit a full bit to a source that carries none alone (Y_t = X_{t−1} ⊕ Y_{t−1}) and report zero from each of two sources that jointly fix the target (Z_t = X_{t−1} ⊕ Y_{t−1}); conditioning on further series, as causation entropy does, has the same fault | James, Barnett & Crutchfield (2016), [LIT-1165](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1165.md), read in full in [NOTE-945](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-945.md). Both examples are exact and were recomputed. The decomposition holds for any PID satisfying the consistency equations. The conclusion is relative to the authors' definition of flow; transfer entropy as predictive improvement is untouched. The claims about directed information, interventional flow and Gaussian systems are cited or conjectured. | Active |
| [THEORY-708](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-708.md) v2 | The I_min redundancy credits two independent sources with shared information whenever each reduces surprise about the same target outcomes, so it gives two independent bits copied into the target 1 bit of redundancy; a bivariate redundancy built from reverse information projections, each source's information less what is lost when its posteriors are replaced by mixtures of the other's, satisfies symmetry, self-redundancy, monotonicity and the identity property, gives a nonnegative decomposition, and agrees with I_min on XOR, AND and their compositions but can reverse the state-independent/state-dependent split of a transfer entropy | Harder, Salge & Polani (2013), [LIT-1168](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1168.md), read in full in [NOTE-944](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-944.md). The counterexample, the axioms and the nonnegativity proof are exact; every Table I value and both transfer-entropy examples were recomputed. The identity axiom and "mechanistic redundancy" are positions, not results, and the measure is bivariate only. | Active |
| [THEORY-709](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-709.md) | Mutual information between continuous variables can be estimated from k-nearest-neighbour statistics, with the joint k-th-neighbour distance in the maximum norm fixing the scale at which marginal neighbours are counted, so that the biases of the three entropy estimates largely cancel; the one approximation is a locally constant density, the systematic error scales with k/N, and exactness for independent variables is observed in every tested case but not proved | Kraskov, Stögbauer & Grassberger (2004), [LIT-1163](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1163.md), read in [NOTE-938](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-938.md) (formal sections in full, numerics at lower resolution). The estimators are derived up to one approximation and one neglected correction; the rest is numerical. Checked by simulation on correlated Gaussians. | Active |
| [THEORY-710](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-710.md) | In a finite causal Bayesian network, a set of nodes is causally independent of another, imposing a third, for every choice of mechanisms exactly when every directed path between them passes through the third; information flow, conditional mutual information computed from interventional instead of observational distributions, vanishes under causal independence, and it can differ from transfer entropy and conditional mutual information in either direction | Ay & Polani (2008), [LIT-1174](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1174.md), read in full in [NOTE-946](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-946.md) from the 2006 preprint. Theorem 2 and Prop. 3 are proved; Examples 3–6 were recomputed. Example 6's one bit holds at k = 1 and fails for k ≥ 2 as stated. The measure needs the mechanisms, and estimation and identification are not addressed. | Active |
| [THEORY-711](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-711.md) | Directed information from an input sequence to an output sequence, the sum over time of the information the inputs up to now carry about the current output given the past outputs, is at most their mutual information and equal to it when the channel is used without feedback; in a causal system it bounds what the output reveals about the source, so feedback cannot raise a memoryless channel's capacity; and the usual definition of a memoryless channel holds only without feedback | Massey (1990), [LIT-1166](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1166.md), read in full in [NOTE-939](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-939.md) from the author's preprint. Three short theorems, all checked; the feedback inequality also checked numerically. "Causal" is Massey's factorization condition, not intervention. That directed information is full-history transfer entropy plus instantaneous terms is the record's derivation. | Active |
| [THEORY-712](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-712.md) v2 | Under any partial information decomposition satisfying the consistency equations, a transfer entropy T_{Y→X} = I(X_{t+1}; Y_t \| X_t) is the unique information of the source's past about the target's next state plus the synergy of source and target pasts, which Williams and Beer call state-independent and state-dependent transfer; time-delayed mutual information is the unique part plus redundancy; with the I_min redundancy the state-independent part alone suffices for perfect open-loop control, and a two-source transfer entropy splits into unique, redundant and synergistic transfer | Williams & Beer (2011), [LIT-1176](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1176.md), an arXiv preprint, read in full in [NOTE-942](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-942.md). The two-term split is an identity from the consistency equations; the sizes of the terms, the control theorem and the multivariate split use I_min, which the record has not read argued for. The one-parameter family and the three corners of the two-source family were recomputed. The text mislabels the synergistic corner. | Active |
| [THEORY-713](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-713.md) | No redundancy measure on the Williams–Beer partial-information lattice can satisfy symmetry, self-redundancy, monotonicity, the identity axiom and non-negative atoms once there are three sources: for two independent bits, their XOR and a target that copies all three, identity forces three one-bit atoms under a two-bit total, so one atom is at most −1 bit, and a multivariate decomposition that keeps identity must give up non-negativity or the lattice | Rauh, Bertschinger, Olbrich & Jost (2014), [LIT-1202](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1202.md), read in full in [NOTE-965](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-965.md). A proved impossibility, checked by hand and by script. It also uses invariance of redundancy under relabelling the target, which is not stated as an axiom. I_min escapes it by failing identity, Ince's I_ccs by accepting the −1-bit atom. | Active |
| [THEORY-715](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-715.md) | The information about a target carried by the Gács–Körner common random variable of the sources is a redundancy defined for any number of sources that is nonnegative, target-monotone and no larger than I_min, and is a lower bound on any reasonable redundancy; but it counts only deterministic shared structure, so it is zero whenever the sources' joint distribution has full support, fails the identity property and continuity, and gives negative synergy already for two sources | Griffith, Chong, James, Ellison & Crutchfield (2014), [LIT-1203](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1203.md), read in full in [NOTE-967](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-967.md). The lemmas are short and exact, and every example was recomputed, with Harder, Salge and Polani's copy family and a three-source copy added. It is the record's one redundancy defined for n > 2, and it does not have the identity property there or for n = 2. | Active |
| [THEORY-716](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-716.md) | Synergy can be measured as the whole minus the union of its parts, the union information being the least information the sources could jointly carry about the target with every source–target marginal held fixed; this synergy lies between WholeMinusSum and Williams and Beer's S_max, which respectively subtract redundancy and count unique information as synergy, and for two sources it is Bertschinger et al.'s synergy, so independent sources can share information about a target, as the authors' last version concedes against their first | Griffith & Koch (2014), [LIT-1204](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1204.md), read in full in [NOTE-966](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-966.md), v6 with v1–v2 checked. The definitions, the criticisms of S_max, WMS and ΔI, and the properties proved in Appendix C are exact, and every Table 1 value for two predictors was recomputed. The identification with Bertschinger et al.'s CI for two sources is the record's derivation. Monotonicity is claimed without proof, and the S_max bound's proof has a step the reading could not reconstruct. | Active |
| [THEORY-717](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-717.md) | For experiments with finitely many states and finitely many outcomes, being at least as informative in every decision problem is the same as being reproducible from the other by a Markov matrix | Blackwell (1953), [LIT-781](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-781.md), Theorems 4–6, read in [NOTE-595](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-595.md): the Sherman– Stein theorem, with a new minimax proof. With n states and finite outcome sets, write experiments as n × N Markov matrices P and Q. Every risk vector Q attains in every decision problem is attainable with P exactly when Q = PM for some Markov matrix M. The arbitrary-outcome extension is [THEORY-156](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md), still Proposed. A qualitative order: most pairs are incomparable, and it says nothing about how far apart they are. | Active |
| [THEORY-718](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-718.md) | In a linear-in-parameters model with Gaussian noise and a Gaussian prior, the evidence is exactly the best-fit likelihood times an Occam factor set by the posterior curvature, and when the design grows linearly with n that factor costs (k/2) log n | MacKay (1992), [LIT-623](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-623.md), Eqs. 5–6 with Eqs. 16 and 19–20, read in [NOTE-471](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-471.md): for y = Φw + noise with Gaussian noise of precision β and the prior w ~ N(0, α⁻¹I) on k weights, the posterior is exactly Gaussian, so the evidence is exactly P(D\|w_MP) times the Occam factor P(w_MP)(2π)^{k/2} det^{-1/2}A, with A = αI + βΦᵀΦ. If ΦᵀΦ/n converges to a positive-definite matrix and w_MP stays bounded, the log Occam factor is −(k/2) log n + O(1). Exact for this model class only. The general regular case and the singular case are [THEORY-087](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-087.md), which is Proposed. | Active |
| [THEORY-719](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-719.md) | On a finite augmentation space, over unconstrained functions of the two views, the spectral contrastive and NT-Logistic losses are both minimized at the positive-pair density ratio | Johnson, El Hanchi & Maddison (2023), [LIT-258](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-258.md), App. B.2–B.3, read in [NOTE-751](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-751.md): on a finite augmentation space, with every function of the two views allowed, the spectral contrastive loss is minimized by K⁺ = p⁺/(p⊗p) exactly, and the NT-Logistic loss with equal positive and negative classes by the log-odds log K⁺, so its exponentiated score is K⁺. Population optima over unconstrained functions only; not what an encoder reaches, and not InfoNCE, which is [THEORY-001](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-001.md)'s open part. | Active |
| [THEORY-720](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-720.md) | Classical simulations between no-signalling empirical models on finite scenarios, which may change the cover, never create contextuality: a model is non-contextual exactly when the empty model simulates it, the non-contextual fraction cannot fall along a simulation, strong contextuality is reflected backwards, and only non-contextual models can be cloned | Karvonen (2018), [LIT-846](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-846.md), Theorems 4.1, 4.3 and 4.5, read in [NOTE-651](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-651.md); Abramsky, Barbosa, Karvonen & Mansfield (2019), [LIT-847](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-847.md), Theorems 21 and 22, read in [NOTE-647](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-647.md). A classical simulation answers each measurement of the target by a jointly measurable set of the source's, with shared classical randomness, so the cover may change. Non-contextual models are exactly those the empty model simulates, NCF cannot fall along a simulation, strong contextuality is reflected backwards, and a model clones itself only if it is non-contextual. No-signalling models on finite scenarios only. Which maps are simulations is [THEORY-174](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-174.md)'s open half. | Active |
| [THEORY-721](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-721.md) | On a complex Hilbert space no orthonormal basis or tensor factorisation of given dimensions is distinguished by the space alone, and orthonormal bases correspond exactly to commutative special †-Frobenius algebras; over the reals that correspondence fails | Three results [THEORY-017](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-017.md) rested on, held apart from its synthesis. (a) The unitary group acts transitively on the orthonormal bases of a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, and on its tensor factorisations of given dimensions, so neither is fixed by the space; a non-degenerate self-adjoint operator fixes a basis up to phases, and its invariant content is its spectrum. (b) Over ℂ, commutative special †-Frobenius algebras correspond exactly to orthonormal bases: Coecke, Pavlovic & Vicary, [LIT-274](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-274.md), Thm 5.1 and §6, in finite dimension; Abramsky & Heunen, [LIT-275](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-275.md), Thm 22, for the non-unital ones satisfying the H*-axiom, in any dimension. (c) Over ℝ it fails: ℂ as a real algebra, with multiplication scaled by 1/√2, is a commutative special †-Frobenius algebra with no nonzero copyable vector. | Active |
| [THEORY-722](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-722.md) | In Contextuality-by-Default 2.0, whether a system of non-binary variables is contextual depends on which variables represent the measurements: coarse-graining can turn a noncontextual system into a contextual one, while for connections of two variables, and for consistently connected systems, CbD 1.0 and 2.0 agree | Dzhafarov & Kujala (2017), [LIT-831](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-831.md), Examples 1–3 and Section 4, read in [NOTE-643](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-643.md) (claims C4 and C6). Under multimaximal couplings, lumping values of non-binary variables can destroy every multimaximal coupling, so a noncontextual system becomes contextual. The verdict on a fixed set of measurements therefore depends on which variables represent them. For connections of two variables, hence cyclic systems, and for consistently connected systems, the 1.0 and 2.0 definitions agree. It does not say the coupling choice changes verdicts in larger connections, which is [THEORY-168](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-168.md)'s asserted part. | Active |
| [THEORY-723](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-723.md) | For the final embedding and unembedding of a softmax model, the output distribution fixes the representations only up to an invertible linear map, and whether closeness in distribution bounds representational dissimilarity depends on the distance: not for KL in the saturation regime, but yes for the log-likelihood variance distance | Nielsen et al. (2025), [LIT-253](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-253.md), read in full in [NOTE-738](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-738.md), with Harvey, Larsen & Williams (2023), [LIT-250](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-250.md), for the kernel side. What is observed fixes a representation only up to that observation's symmetry group: a centred linear kernel up to a translation and an orthogonal map ([THEORY-004](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-004.md)), and a softmax output distribution up to an invertible linear map of the embedding with the inverse transpose on the unembedding (Thm 2.2). KL can go to zero while the embeddings stay non-linearly related (Thm 3.1, Cor. 3.2), but d_LLV ≤ ε gives d_f,g ≤ 2Mε (Thm 4.7). Final layer only. It does not say what the Platonic hypothesis means; that is [THEORY-002](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-002.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-724](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-724.md) | For a linear system du/dt = A(t)u, non-normality is necessary for time dependence to destabilize an operator that is uniformly stable at every instant, and a non-normal operator neutral at every instant can be asymptotically unstable under switching | Farrell & Ioannou (1996), Part II, [LIT-929](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-929.md), eq. 12 and §4, read in [NOTE-842](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-842.md). Because d‖u‖²/dt = u†(A + A†)u, the first Lyapunov exponent lies between the long-run averages of the extreme eigenvalues of the Hermitian part. For a normal operator the largest is the spectral abscissa, so an operator that is normal and uniformly stable at every instant has a negative exponent. A switched undamped oscillator, neutral at every instant, has a positive exponent. The stochastic genericity results are [THEORY-325](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-325.md)'s, still Proposed. | Active |
| [THEORY-725](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-725.md) | On the court agenda {P, Q, R, R iff (P and Q)} under universal domain, proposition-wise majority voting is not robustly rational, while the premise-based procedure is, and it makes the group's judgments a function of the members' whole judgment sets that the members' judgments on the conclusion neither fix nor need to enter | List & Pettit (2006), [LIT-705](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-705.md), read in full in [NOTE-550](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-550.md), for the court agenda only. Proposition 1: majority voting on each proposition is not robustly rational, by the discursive dilemma. Proposition 4: the premise-based procedure, majorities on P, Q and the biconditional with R derived, is robustly rational and makes the group's set a function of the members' sets. Under it the members' judgments on R do not fix the group's (weak discontinuity), and under the distributed procedure they need not enter (strong discontinuity, Proposition 5). The general impossibility for proposition-wise rules is [THEORY-127](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-127.md), still Proposed. | Active |
| [THEORY-726](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-726.md) | Weight decay on factors is a nuclear-norm penalty on their product: with tied weights λ‖W‖²_F = λ‖WWᵀ‖_*, and for untied factors the least (‖U‖²_F + ‖V‖²_F)/2 over UVᵀ = M is ‖M‖_*, so for any loss that sees the weights only through the product, square-penalized training is nuclear-norm-penalized training of a product of bounded rank | Boncoraglio et al. (2025), [LIT-857](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-857.md), Appendix A, read in [NOTE-661](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-661.md), and re-derived here. ‖W‖²_F = Tr(WWᵀ) = ‖WWᵀ‖_*, since a PSD matrix's singular values are its eigenvalues. For untied factors, Hölder's inequality for Schatten norms and AM–GM bound ‖M‖_* by (‖U‖²_F + ‖V‖²_F)/2 over every factorization UVᵀ = M, and the balanced SVD factorization attains it. The product's rank is bounded by the factors' inner dimension. It says nothing about what the trained product looks like, which is [THEORY-180](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-180.md)'s spectral law. | Active |
| [THEORY-727](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-727.md) | For a fixed linear operator in an inner-product norm, growth over time t is the top singular value of the propagator, which the eigenvalues bound only from below; it starts at the numerical abscissa, which can be positive when every mode decays; and the forced response is bounded by the condition number of the eigenvectors over the distance to the spectrum | Farrell & Ioannou (1996), [LIT-931](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-931.md), read in [NOTE-831](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-831.md), with Trefethen et al. (1993), [LIT-932](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-932.md), read in [NOTE-839](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-839.md). For du/dt = Au with A fixed: a normal A grows as its spectral abscissa; in general the growth over t is σ_max(e^(At)), with the eigenvalues as a floor; the initial growth rate is the top eigenvalue of (A + A†)/2; and harmonic forcing is bounded by κ(E)/dist(iω, Λ(A)), with the ε-pseudospectrum marking where eigenvalues of A + Δ, ‖Δ‖ < ε, can go. All in a chosen norm. The white-noise variance result is [THEORY-323](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-323.md)'s, still Proposed. | Active |
| [THEORY-728](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-728.md) | On a finite data set, a symmetric positive affinity normalized to a Markov operator is conjugate to a symmetric one, and its eigenvectors scaled by powers of their eigenvalues embed the data so that Euclidean distance equals the diffusion distance weighted by the inverse stationary law | Coifman et al. (2005), [LIT-981](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-981.md), skimmed in [NOTE-784](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-784.md), with the derivation written out here because the paper's equations were not seen. For n points and a symmetric affinity K with positive entries, A = D⁻¹K is a Markov matrix with stationary law π ∝ d. It is conjugate to the symmetric D^(-1/2) K D^(-1/2), so its eigenvalues are real and in [−1, 1], and in [0, 1] when K is positive semi-definite. The map x ↦ (λ_j^m ψ_j(x))_{j≥1} turns the m-step diffusion distance, weighted by 1/π, into Euclidean distance exactly. Truncation gives a lower bound. It says nothing about the continuum limit, which is [THEORY-565](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-565.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-729](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-729.md) | An adjunction between a category and the opposite of another restricts to a dual equivalence between the full subcategories on which its unit and counit are isomorphisms | Corfield (2017), [LIT-115](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-115.md), §3, read in full in [NOTE-141](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-141.md), with the proof the paper omits written out here. For F : C → D^op left adjoint to G : D^op → C, let C′ and D′ be the full subcategories on which the unit and the counit are isomorphisms. Then F and G restrict to inverse equivalences C′ ≃ D′, and D′ is a full subcategory of D^op, so C′ is dually equivalent to a full subcategory of D. Pontrjagin duality is the example. That most dualities are of this form is [THEORY-604](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-604.md)'s thesis, still Proposed. | Active |
| [THEORY-730](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-730.md) | For an embedding whose Gram matrix is the absolute co-occurrence deviation matrix at full rank, words on a periodic lattice whose positive and negative co-occurrence parts each depend only on separation have Fourier modes of the lattice as principal components, in degenerate cos/sin pairs with amplitude the square root of the kernel's Fourier transform, and the exponential kernel gives a closed loop with integer frequencies on a periodic lattice and an open curve with non-integer frequencies on an interval | Karkada, Korchinski, Nava, Wyart & Bahri (2026), [LIT-860](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-860.md), Propositions 1, 3 and 4 and Corollary 2, with the proofs in Appendix E followed in [NOTE-664](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-664.md). The result is conditional throughout. It concerns an idealised embedding with W Wᵀ = \|M*\| and d ≥ rank M*, not a trained one. It needs the positive and negative parts of M* to be translation invariant separately (Assumption B.1), not M* alone. It says nothing about whether any corpus or model satisfies these conditions, which is [THEORY-183](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-183.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-731](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-731.md) | For softmax cross-entropy with balanced classes, the Gauss–Newton matrix splits exactly into four positive semidefinite second-moment terms, the class-centre term has rank at most C with eigenvectors in the span of the class centres and the spectrum of a C × C Gram matrix, and so the k-th eigenvalue of the whole is never below the k-th eigenvalue of the class-centre term | Papyan (2019), [LIT-619](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-619.md), read in [NOTE-479](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-479.md). Exact algebra, re-derived here. For softmax cross-entropy, the Gauss–Newton matrix is G = (1/n)ΔΔᵀ, an uncentred second moment of logit derivatives indexed by class and logit. Grouping them gives G = G₀ + G₁ + G₂ + G₃, with every term positive semidefinite. G₁, the class-centre term, has rank at most C, and its spectrum is read from a C × C Gram matrix. So λ_k(G) ≥ λ_k(G₁ + G₂) ≥ λ_k(G₁) for every k, in any network, trained or not. That G₁ carries the outliers of trained networks is measured, not derived, and stays Proposed in [THEORY-078](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-078.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-732](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-732.md) | For ReLU networks interpolated linearly between two endpoints, weak additivity and commutativity at every layer make each layer's features exactly the interpolation of the endpoints' features, output-layer linearity bounds the path's error by twice the endpoints', and for one hidden layer with interpolating minima linear mode connectivity alone gives the exact case | Zhou et al. (2023), [LIT-674](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-674.md), read in [NOTE-512](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-512.md) with Appendix A's proofs checked: for an L-layer ReLU MLP on a finite dataset, weak additivity of ReLU over the two networks' pre-activations and the commutativity W_A H_B + W_B H_A = W_A H_A + W_B H_B at every layer make the interpolated network's features at every layer exactly the interpolation of the endpoints' features (Theorem 1). Output-layer linearity, at any positive scale, keeps the path's error within twice the endpoints' (Lemma 1). Lubana et al. (2022), [LIT-669](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-669.md), Lemma 2: for one hidden layer and interpolating minima, linear mode connectivity forces shared activation patterns, and with shared patterns the hidden features are linear along the path. It says nothing about when the conditions hold. That trained pairs satisfy them is [THEORY-111](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-111.md)'s empirical claim. | Active |
| [THEORY-733](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-733.md) | For a stable linear Gaussian VAR(p), a linear coarse-graining is exactly dynamically independent iff its row space is invariant under the transpose of every lag matrix, so for p ≥ 2 almost no parameter set has one at any scale, while for p = 1 they are the transpose's invariant subspaces, which exist on open sets but not generically at every scale | Barnett and Seth (2023), [LIT-979](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-979.md), read in [NOTE-791](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-791.md): the VAR form (3.26) of exact dynamical independence, with the genericity count of §3.3 made a proof for VAR order p ≥ 2 and corrected for p = 1. Linear coarse-grainings Y = LX of a stable VAR with non-degenerate Gaussian innovations only. It says nothing about near-independence, about the multimodality of the dynamical-dependence cost, or about nonlinear maps. | Active |
| [THEORY-734](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-734.md) | In the hyperbolic plane, a root carrying deg_max ≥ 15 chains of length m, embedded with worst-case distortion 1 + ε for ε ≤ 1, forces some node to hyperbolic distance at least (ℓ/(4ε))·ln(deg_max/(π√2)) from the origin, so fixed-point Poincaré coordinates need Ω((ℓ/ε) log deg_max) bits | Sala, De Sa, Gu and Ré (2018), [LIT-874](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-874.md), Lemma D.1, read in [NOTE-679](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-679.md), with the proof redone here without the paper's small-angle approximation. Only the root's children are used to fix the embedding's scale c, and then the chains turn the scale into depth. Plane only, one family of trees, fixed-point coordinates in the Poincaré disk, deg_max ≥ 15 and ε ≤ 1. It says nothing about H^r for r > 2, or about whether any tree needs fewer bits under another number system. | Active |
| [THEORY-735](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-735.md) | Under a local quadratic model of the loss with the greedy optimal step, per-step progress at batch size B is ΔL_max/(1 + B_noise/B), and at fixed B the steps and examples needed satisfy (S/S_min − 1)(E/E_min − 1) = 1, with E_min/S_min the progress-weighted mean of B_noise | McCandlish, Kaplan, Amodei et al. (2018), [LIT-348](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-348.md), §2 and App. D.1, as read and re-derived in [NOTE-293](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-293.md). A derivation under stated assumptions: a second-order model of the loss along the step, an unbiased minibatch gradient of covariance Σ/B, and the step size that maximises the expected decrease. It says nothing about whether real training meets those assumptions, or how well the noise scale predicts the measured critical batch, which is [THEORY-033](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-033.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-736](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-736.md) | Two ε-dropout-stable solutions of a multilayer ReLU net, under a loss convex in the output, are joined by a piecewise-linear path whose loss never exceeds the worse endpoint's by more than ε, and joined pairwise paths compose with no higher barrier than their worst | Kuditipudi et al. (2019), [LIT-671](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-671.md), Theorem 1, read in full in [NOTE-544](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-544.md), with Draxler et al.'s (2018) concatenation bound from [LIT-653](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-653.md). Dropout stability gives every solution a half-width copy with the same loss up to ε. Half the units are then free, so working units can be swapped in and permuted at no cost. That joins any two such solutions. It is a statement about dropout-stable solutions only: whether training produces them is [THEORY-109](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-109.md)'s open question, and Theorem 4 of the same paper builds disconnected global minima. | Active |
| [THEORY-737](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-737.md) | In a spectral contrastive graph that joins labelled known classes to unlabelled data, the least-squares residual of a novel labelling on the top-k eigenspace, with the labelled entries left free, equals exactly the part of the labelling outside that eigenspace that the labelled rows of the discarded eigenvectors cannot absorb | Sun, Shi, Liang & Li (2023), [LIT-235](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-235.md), Theorem 5.5 with its proof in C.1, read in [NOTE-833](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-833.md). The paper states the identity as ≤, and its proof is a chain of equalities. Re-derived here in three steps from orthogonality and least squares. With the paper's Lemma 5.1 it bounds the novel labelling's 0–1 linear-probe error by twice this residual. It is about the exact rank-k factorization of a population graph, not about trained networks. | Active |
| [THEORY-738](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-738.md) | In the unconstrained-features max-margin problem with k classes under step imbalance and feature dimension at least k − 1, the unique optimal logits are the simplex-encoded labels, every margin equals one, and the classifier and embedding Gram matrices are the two square-root factors of that matrix's singular value decomposition; the geometry is the simplex equiangular tight frame exactly when the classes are balanced or there are two of them | Thrampoulidis, Kini, Vakilian and Behnia (2022), [LIT-994](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-994.md), Theorem 1 and Corollary 1.3, read in [NOTE-764](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-764.md) and re-derived here. By [THEORY-726](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-726.md) the problem is nuclear-norm minimisation of the logits under margin constraints. The polar factor of the simplex-encoded label matrix certifies it optimal, because under step imbalance its off-diagonal entries are negative. It does not say that gradient descent or trained networks reach this geometry, which is [THEORY-286](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-286.md)'s. | Active |
| [THEORY-739](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-739.md) | For the quartic proxy of word2vec with tied weights, symmetric reweighting and constant weights, the rank-d minimisers are the top d eigenvectors of the relative deviation-from-independence matrix M*, scaled by the square roots of their eigenvalues, up to rotation; and from an initialisation aligned with those eigenvectors, gradient flow acquires each one in an independent logistic rise, in order of eigenvalue | Karkada, Simon, Bahri and DeWeese (2025), [LIT-855](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-855.md), Theorem 1 and Proposition 2, read in [NOTE-660](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-660.md) and re-derived here. The quartic proxy is a function of WWᵀ alone, so von Neumann's trace inequality gives its rank-d minimisers. Gradient flow from an aligned start keeps the eigenbasis and reduces each mode to a logistic equation. It does not say that word2vec, or the proxy from random initialisation, behaves this way; that is [THEORY-182](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-182.md)'s. | Active |
| [THEORY-740](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-740.md) | A two-layer linear network trained by gradient flow on white inputs from a decoupled, balanced start learns each singular mode of its input–output correlation in a logistic rise that waits a time of order its inverse strength times the log of the inverse initial scale, so the modes arrive one at a time in order of strength; a single-layer network on the same data learns every mode on one timescale with no plateau, so under these conditions the stages come from the product of layers and the data's spectrum | Saxe, McClelland and Ganguli (2014, 2019), [LIT-864](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-864.md) and [LIT-862](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-862.md), read in [NOTE-667](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-667.md) and [NOTE-666](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-666.md), re-derived here. From a decoupled, balanced start the two-layer equations keep the SVD basis of Σyx, and each mode's strength obeys τȧ = 2a(s − a), a logistic rise. One weight matrix on the same data relaxes every mode exponentially on the one timescale τ. It does not say that random starts follow the solution, which is [THEORY-186](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-186.md)'s. | Active |
